Gunpowder Ooze.name: Gunpowder Ooze
Gunpowder Ooze.publicNotes:
Gunpowder oozes are explosive gunpowder given life. By necessity, crafters of explosives and firearms are a careful lot, but even the best safety habits can be thwarted by greed, distraction, or carelessness. The release of toxic byproducts from gunsmithing would be an environmental problem anywhere, but when volatile runoff seeps into the Mana Wastes, it can INTERACT with wild magic, causing a living, explosive nightmare.

A gunpowder ooze is a pockmarked, charcoal gray mass that slithers across the blighted verge between Alkenstar and the Mana Wastes with the sound of sizzles and sudden pops. It pursues and consumes any sort of organic matter, firing bullet-like projectiles to bring down prey. The ooze instinctively avoids fire, so travelers forced to camp in known gunpowder ooze territory often light bonfires despite the danger of advertising their presence to the Mana Wastes' other residents. Suggestions that local populations of oozes be weaponized, periodically put forward by unwise Alkenstari and Mana Waste tacticians, are uniformly shot down by cooler heads; those who attempt to proceed anyway usually meet explosive ends.

action->Motion Sense.name: Motion Sense
action->Motion Sense.description: A gunpowder ooze can sense nearby criaturas through vibration and air or water movement.

action->Combust.name: Combust
action->Combust.description: Due to the volatile NATURE of its composition, the gunpowder ooze reacts explosively when exposed to open flame. Any time the gunpowder ooze takes daño de fuego from a source other than a gunpowder ooze's combust or gunpowder residue, it explodes, dealing @Damage[15d6[fire]|options:area-damage] daño to criaturas in a @Template[emanation|distance:15] including itself (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect]). When the gunpowder ooze combusts, it automatically splits as long as it has 10 or more HP.

action->Split.name: Split
action->Split.description: When a gunpowder ooze that has 10 or more HP is hit by an attack that would deal slashing or daño perforante, it splits into two identical oozes, each with half the original's HP. One ooze is in the same space as the original, and the other is in an adjacent, unoccupied space. If no adjacent space is unoccupied, it automatically pushes criaturas and objects out of the way to fill a space (the GM decides if an object or criatura is too big or heavy to push).

action->Gunpowder Residue.name: Gunpowder Residue
action->Gunpowder Residue.description: A criatura hit by the gunpowder ooze's pseudopod or blast is coated in explosive material unless it succeeds at a @Check[reflex|dc:34] salvación. If a criatura makes an attack with a firearm, takes daño de fuego, or uses an action, activity, or item with the fire rasgo while coated with the residue, the residue explodes, dealing @Damage[7d6[fire]] daño to the criatura and all adjacent criaturas (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic]). The residue remains active for 24 horas, until it's ignited, or until it's scrubbed off (an activity that takes at least 10 minutos and requires soap and water). A criatura can only be coated with one layer of gunpowder residue at a time.

Hellknight Armiger.name: Hellknight Armiger
Hellknight Armiger.publicNotes:
Este menacing dwarf wears a suit of armor emblazoned with the symbol of her Hellknight order, and she wields a mighty flail.

Armigers are the pies soldiers of the Hellknights and form the largest group of members for most orders. Whatever their specific reasons for joining the organization, armigers share the Hellknights' dedication to spreading the rule of law across Golarion. Este commitment sees them serving in a variety of missions, whether it be rooting out bandits and crooks, imprisoning smugglers and black marketeers, or investigating rumors of sedition. While frontier villagers sometimes welcome the assurance of safety that the Hellknights bring, free thinkers and historians chafe at the restrictions on movement and expression that armigers enforce.

Although armigers are not yet full knights, those who underestimate them have made a grievous error. Once ordered to take a position or eliminate a foe, an armiger is unerring in fulfilling their order. During battle, they wade eagerly into the fray, targeting servants of chaotic gods and those they observe using underhanded tactics.

Firm believers in enforcing the law at any cost, Hellknights are often based in Cheliax, but they travel to all across Golarion to enforce their ideals of order. Este rigid viewpoint and intolerance for dissent means that PCs can just as easily find villains in these Hellknights as they can allies; an agent of the Hellknight Order of the Chain might aid the PCs in subduing a vile and violent criminal, or might hunt down the PCs due to mild infractions of unjust laws. The Hellknight armiger presented here might be an unrepentant enforcer seeking to quell rebellion among the oppressed, a dedicated monster hunter, a censor of artistic innovation, a savior to victims of kidnapping, a spy and torturer, or a lawful crusader against demonic incursions. Hellknight paravicars, meanwhile, are absolute exemplars of their orders, and PCs who encounter them will likely find themselves in the midst of momentous events.

Hellknight Paravicar.name: Hellknight Paravicar
Hellknight Paravicar.publicNotes:
Face covered by a menacing helm and body clad in ornate plate, this figure projects an aura of immutable authority.

Each order of Hellknights is led by a powerful paravicar, a general in charge of dictating the order's tactics and the administration of its resources. Within the order, the word of these figures is law, and members from the lowliest squire to the most senior knight follow commands from a paravicar with unswerving devotion. Paravicars see their personal dedication to the order's edicts as an example for all members and hold themselves to the same high standards as their underlings. Though they seldom need to call upon them, paravicars use their considerable infernal powers to reinforce their positions in the Hellknight's hierarchy.

In combat, paravicars take direct command of their troops of knights and armigers. Paravicars are experienced campaigners who prefer calculated tactical gambits to hot-headed, risky maneuvers that could leave their forces exposed. If pressed into combat, paravicars use their abilities to DEMORALIZE their foes and compel enemies to become their allies or to flee the field.

Firm believers in enforcing the law at any cost, Hellknights are often based in Cheliax, but they travel to all across Golarion to enforce their ideals of order. Este rigid viewpoint and intolerance for dissent means that PCs can just as easily find villains in these Hellknights as they can allies; an agent of the Hellknight Order of the Chain might aid the PCs in subduing a vile and violent criminal, or might hunt down the PCs due to mild infractions of unjust laws. The Hellknight armiger presented here might be an unrepentant enforcer seeking to quell rebellion among the oppressed, a dedicated monster hunter, a censor of artistic innovation, a savior to victims of kidnapping, a spy and torturer, or a lawful crusader against demonic incursions. Horned Archdragon.name: Horned Archdragon
Horned Archdragon.publicNotes:
The magic that flows through primal dragons can manifest more animalistic or bestial features in a given type of dragon. Notably among these are the massive paired horns of the horned dragon. While their bulky frames, natural coloration, and prominent ridged scales are all remarkable in their own way, it's the horns that are most obvious and striking at first glance. Horned dragons use their horns to impale their prey in a quick and brutal display of their might. They are generally contemplative and have a fixation on knowledge and self-discipline, rasgos belied by their bestial appearance. As a result, horned dragons are generally more open to speaking with outsiders.

Dragons come in myriad forms, with many having magical abilities or connections to magic. Some dragons draw greater power from magic than others, allowing them to manifest abilities or alter their physiques with prolonged exposure to magic. Estos dragons become more powerful as they age and strengthen their connections with their magical origins. Scholars debate the classification of these dragons, with some preferring the name magical dragons and others using traditional dragons due to their connection to specific magical traditions. Regardless of their names, these dragons share a number of characteristics: their ability to tap into magical energies, intensified might and cunning as they grow older, and an inclination to hoard vast amounts of treasure and wealth.

Horned Archdragon (Spellcaster).name: Horned Archdragon (Spellcaster)
Horned Archdragon (Spellcaster).publicNotes:
The magic that flows through primal dragons can manifest more animalistic or bestial features in a given type of dragon. Notably among these are the massive paired horns of the horned dragon. While their bulky frames, natural coloration, and prominent ridged scales are all remarkable in their own way, it's the horns that are most obvious and striking at first glance. Horned dragons use their horns to impale their prey in a quick and brutal display of their might. They are generally contemplative and have a fixation on knowledge and self-discipline, rasgos belied by their bestial appearance. As a result, horned dragons are generally more open to speaking with outsiders.

Dragons come in myriad forms, with many having magical abilities or connections to magic. Some dragons draw greater power from magic than others, allowing them to manifest abilities or alter their physiques with prolonged exposure to magic. Estos dragons become more powerful as they age and strengthen their connections with their magical origins. Scholars debate the classification of these dragons, with some preferring the name magical dragons and others using traditional dragons due to their connection to specific magical traditions. Regardless of their names, these dragons share a number of characteristics: their ability to tap into magical energies, intensified might and cunning as they grow older, and an inclination to hoard vast amounts of treasure and wealth.

Ijhyeojin.name: Ijhyeojin
Ijhyeojin.publicNotes:
Ijhyeojins (ee-jyuh-jeens) fueron once joseung sajas, psychopomps who guided el muerto a el Boneyard as divino punishment for su sins. Over time, ellos rejected su roles y became sakhils. Some did este due a un sentido de injustice over having a atone for su sins en el afterlife, but todos do so partially out de un desperate desire a reclaim su memories—for ijhyeojins son named for el fear ellos manifest, el fear de being forgotten. They prey en people who son socially isolated by circumstances o those obsessed con su legacy, slowly cutting su victims off de friends, professional contacts, y family. Ijhyeojins particularly enjoy infiltrating medical facilities a prey en patients who fear about being forgotten en su deaths, snatching away crucial memories de them o su visiting loved ones. Hunting en este way also grants el sahkils ideal positioning a lure joseung sajas a su demise.

Ijhyeojins resemble el pale-skinned psychopomps ellos used a be, except su faces tienen no distinguishable features, like un skull con un smooth layer de piel pulled over ello. Their bodies continue a twist y grow el longer ellos live.
Ijhyeojin.privateNotes:
Fatal Feud

Ijhyeojins regard todos joseung sajas as brainwashed servants de el Boneyard who need a be "awakened" de su sentido de duty through fear. Despite su perception de themselves as liberators, ijhyeojins delight en watching un joseung saja unravel completely as ellos quedan consumed y reborn as faceless sakhils by su own fear.

Imugi.name: Imugi
Imugi.publicNotes:
Imugi (ee-moo-ghee) are dragon-like serpents with great mystic potential, including that of ascension into another form. While some imperial dragons are born to their birthright, many that currently roam Tian Xia are ascended imugi—though they would strike down anyone who claimed such.

To become an imperial dragon, imugi must care for a koi egg for a thousand years. The power from the nurtured egg hatching is enough to power a draconic ascension ritual, and whatever power lingers transforms the koi into an imugi to continue the cycle. The kind of imperial dragon that the imugi becomes depends on where it chooses to nurture the koi egg. Imugi strongly prefer long-finned koi, and Tian koi farmers have learned to keep a separate pool of these butterfly koi away from the others they tend, as imugi tend to displace quite a bit of water—and koi—when swooping down to snatch an egg they want.

Though imugi have some power over rain and storms, most aren't powerful enough to exact a true sense of weather control. Many are known for their benevolence, and some villages even rely on imugi's forays out of streams or lakes, bringing rains during the growing season. Imugi have as wide a range of temperaments as the dragons they become, and some are notorious for how their impatience twists into a foul temper or an arrogance that flicks people aside as if they were bugs. While some might consider mean-spirited imugi corrupted and claim they can be purified somehow, imugi simply hold themselves higher than the average criatura and see no reason to conceal their true NATURE from someone they see as beneath them.
Imugi.privateNotes:
Imperial Ascension

El ritual un imugi undergoes a quedan un true dragon releases un burst de overwhelming magia. Characters exposed a este burst might find su minds filled con lost techniques o abilities que el imugi tiene encountered over su long life, allowing them a obtienen access a uncommon o rare character options, suddenly understand formulas a craft objetos, o immediately retrain along un nuevo path

Mientras su efforts tienen mostly been focused en liberating rural communities en el nation's outskirts thus far, ellos tienen also begun targeted strikes against mercenary bands y supply caravans traveling through Nidal en su way a aid el Chelaxian war effort.

Irriseni Owlbear.name: Osobúho irrisenio
Irriseni Owlbear.publicNotes:
A cultural symbol for Irrisen, the Irriseni owlbear is particularly well adapted to frosty conditions. Estos owlbears are larger than their temperate zone counterparts.

With the body of a powerful brown bear and the keen senses of an owl, the owlbear is a dangerous territorial predator, fearlessly attacking any criatura that strays into its domain. Those who run afoul of an owlbear hear its terrifying screech only seconds before the massive criatura is upon them, ripping them apart with deadly talons and a powerful beak.

Although their origin is lost to time, owlbears are assumed to be the result of a magical experiment to make a more cunning predator. According to the legend, the wizard was too successful and ended up being the flrst victim of the beast. Today, owlbears can be found around the world, with a variety of features. While the most common subspecies looks like a brown bear with the features of a great horned owl, owlbears from the frozen north might resemble polar bears mixed with snowy owls, and in temperate rain forests they might resemble black bears with the heads of barn owls.

Most owlbears live solitary lives, gathering only to mate and raise cubs, which are hatched from eggs. An owlbear's territory usually extends to around 5 miles from its lair, with clear signs of its habitat appearing with 1 mile (clawed up trees, gigantic feathers, and shredded carcasses). The lair of an owlbear rarely holds anything of value, but some adventurers have found trinkets, coins, and even jewelry in the massive pellets of undigested bones these monsters leave behind.

action->Bloodcurdling Screech.name: Bloodcurdling Screech
action->Bloodcurdling Screech.description:

Jiidon.name: Jiidon
Jiidon.publicNotes:
Legends among jiidons explain that many ages ago, when magic was wilder and of less distinct order, a magic-touched rat consumed the discarded fingernails of a human, and the gods granted that rat the ability to shapeshift into a copy of that human. True or not, jiidons are seemingly normal rats who share the blessing from this story. It's unclear where the first jiidon was born because their descendants live among rat and humanoid populations around the world. In their original forms, jiidons are extremely difficult to distinguish from an ordinary rat and often even finds a home leading its non-sapient kin.

After eating the discarded fingernails of a humanoid, however, a jiidon can assume the shape of the clippings' owner, resembling the subject in all of the obvious and superficial ways, with several subtle differences. Their ears are a little larger and sometimes come to a small point. Their teeth continue to grow for their entire lifetimes, so they must regularly chew on stones, bark, and other hard materials to file their teeth down and conceal their true NATURE. The whiskers that grow from the sides of their faces also require daily trimming.

Jiidons are mostly harmless, but their powers provoke alarm among those who know of them. Mothers scold their children not to clip their nails after nightfall, lest a lurking jiidon seize a sliver that got lost in the dark. Though as cautious as any rat, most jiidons want nothing more than to transform and take a place in humanoid SOCIETY. In order to reduce suspicion, they've been known to target those who are unpopular among their neighbors. The gratitude they feel when they do replace a humanoid can sometimes be seen in their actions, revealing the fact that el objetivo has been replaced or endearing jiidons to those who didn't appreciate the original's attitude.

Jiidons from large families will often seek a role that grants them access to nail trimmings, such as a cleaner or doctor, and pass the gift of humanoid form through the family.
Jiidon.privateNotes:
Playing un Jiidon

Mientras jiidons don't tienen ancestral rules en este book, un player interested en creating un jiidon character puede usar el beastkin versatile heritage a emulate un jiidon who tiene obtained un permanent humanoide form. El player should work con el DJ a determine who el jiidon es imitating y what complications este might tienen.

action->Scurrying Retreat.description:

Efecto The jiidon reverts to their rat form and Climbs or Strides. They can't resume humanoid form for 1 minuto.

action->Consumed Fragments.name: Consumed Fragments
action->Consumed Fragments.description: The jiidon takes on the form of any Medium or Small humanoid criatura whose fingernails or similar fragments they've consumed within the last week, gaining the effects of a 3rd-rank illusory disguise conjuro to impersonate the criatura for 8 hours; this is a polymorph effect rather than an illusion effect. Once a jiidon has transformed into a criatura in this way, they must eat that criatura's fingernails again to transform into it again. If a jiidon consumes the nails of a specific humanoid three nights in a row, they can take the form of that humanoid at will but can't use this ability to imitate any other humanoid thereafter.

action->Tactical Gnaw.name: Tactical Gnaw
action->Tactical Gnaw.description: The jiidon uses their nearly indestructible teeth to chew through even the toughest armor, leaving an opponent vulnerable. The jiidon makes a jaws Golpe. On a successful attack, if el objetivo is wearing armor with Hardness 10 or lower, the armor becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6dNUvdb1dhToNDj3]{Broken}. Este Golpe doesn't further daño armor that's already broken.

Joseung Saja.name: Joseung Saja
Joseung Saja.publicNotes:
Joseung saja (jo-seung sah-jah) is a name sometimes bestowed on criaturas in the afterlife who have committed grave sins in their lifetimes. Known also as reapers, these pale and sunken-eyed criaturas are psychopomps—beings who guide the souls of the dead to the Boneyard. No one knows the specific criteria for one to become joseung sajas, but those who are selected have their memories erased and must work as joseung sajas until they've been deemed to have fully atoned for their sins.

Joseung sajas from different eras wander the world, and when a criatura nears death, one will appear and await el objetivo's demise as their afterlife guide. When needed, they even alter their target's memories to remove painful emotions that might chain them to the mortal world, easing them into a peaceful death. Este duty prevents those who die tragic or violent deaths from becoming bound to the world as ghosts—a mercy, though one often unappreciated by the wards of joseung sajas. If a criatura targeted by a joseung saja becomes undead or otherwise cheats death, the reaper must fulfill their duty of granting the criatura a true death.

Because joseung sajas linger among mortals in order to perform their duties, they're one of the most commonly seen psychopomps.
Joseung Saja.privateNotes:
Death-long Career

Even after atoning for their sins and regaining their memories, some souls elige to retain their titles as joseung sajas. Estos experienced reapers hunt ijhyeojin, former joseung sajas who have abandoned their posts. To joseung sajas, an ijhyeojin is no more than just another soul overstaying its welcome in the world of the living.

K'nonna.name: K'nonna
K'nonna.publicNotes:
K'nonna are half human-and only half, in the most literal sense. They most often resemble the right half of a human, and less frequently the left half, split perfectly down the middle starting at the crown of their head. They accordingly have one eye, one ear, one arm, one leg, half of a nose, and half of a mouth full of razor-sharp teeth. A faint shimmer in the air, like the waves over a hot stone, hints at where their other half would be.

Despite the bizarre appearance of the k'nonna, they have no trouble balancing or performing everyday tasks that might be impeded by missing half of their bodies. They are extremely dexterous, able to perform complex tasks with only a single hand. The NATURE of their missing half has so far defied explanation; it is not invisible, nor does it exist on another plane, yet it seems to exert enough force for a k'nonna to walk like a human being.

No one is certain of the k'nonna's origins, except that they are not of this world and not descended from any known mortal criatura. Banishment magic has no effect on them, implying they do not come from another plane. They are intelligent but difficult to communicate with-they speak only in half words and hear only half of what anyone says. K'nonna are also much less interested in talking than eating, and humanoids happen to be their favorite meal. The remains of a k'nonna's victim are unmistakable, as they only consume half the body.

Stories tell of the half-people's love for gifts, especially jewelry. Offerings of rings and necklaces easily distract a k'nonna long enough for prey to escape. Particularly bold victims might try to trick a k'nonna into wearing a bracelet that binds their one visible wrist or ankle to immobilize them, though the tactic is not foolproof, as a k'nonna displeased with their gifts will hunt the person who displeased them for the rest of their days.

action->Gilded Fascination.name: Gilded Fascination
action->Gilded Fascination.description:
When offered a gift worth at least 50 gp, the k'nonna must attempt a @Check[will|dc:20] tirada de salvación; if the gift is worth at least 100 gp, the DC is instead @Check[will|dc:25|name:Gilded Fascination (Higher)].

If they fail the save, the k'nonna accepts the gift, becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} until the end of their next turn, and cannot attack while fascinated. On a critical failure, the fascination lasts for 1 minuto.

Offering a gift is an INTERACT action, and offering multiple gifts in the same round has no additional effect.

action->Half Steps.name: Half Steps
action->Half Steps.description: Even though k'nonna are split in half, they still move and Zancada as though they have two arms and legs. However, binding just one wrist or ankle leaves them incapable of using that limb, as if it were bound to another.

action->Half-Speaker.name: Half-Speaker
action->Half-Speaker.description:
A k'nonna can communicate easily with other k'nonna, but when communicating with other criaturas, only half of the spoken words make sense.

In order to convey information to a k'nonna or understand what they're saying, a non-k'nonna must succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check.

action->Pounce.name: Pounce
action->Pounce.description: The k'nonna Strides and makes a Golpe at the end of that movement. If the k'nonna began this action hidden, they remain hidden until after this ability's Golpe.

Kaava Stalker.name: Acechador Kaava
Kaava Stalker.publicNotes:
Kaava hunting parties puede number en el dozens, although ellos blend easily into el bosque y cobertura todos traces de su passage. Mientras community elders assign various tasks a hunting parties, such as recovering food o deterring intruders, el parties son expected a accomplish these tasks as ellos see fit.

Kaava son stealthy, jungla-dwelling humanoides con short down feathers que puede easily be mistaken for fur de un distance. Kaava tienen tough scales beneath these feathers. Both el scales y feathers tienen mutable pigmentation que allows un kaava a blend into surrounding follaje like un chameleon.

Kallas Devil.publicNotes: Bearing a resemblance to the flayed nuckelavee that lurks in stagnant swamps, the Kallas Devil distinguishes herself by being able to separate herself from her mount without issue, as well as with her powers of disguise and subtlety. Though her wicked trident and violent fury are enough to sear her image into the minds of the local people, it's the Kallas Devil's ability to slip unseen among her would-be victims that elevates the criatura beyond the ranks of a common horror. No matter how careful the residents of Riverton are with their youth and the vulnerable, the Kallas Devil claims her chosen target more often than not, luring the hapless victim toward doom while wearing a smiling child's face.

Karina.name: Karina
Karina.publicNotes:
Karinas-also known as plague birds-are large owl-like criaturas with dark red feathers, powerful talons, and unsettling eyes. Their broad wings conceal a pair of wiry humanoid arms that end in clawed fingers, which they use to dig through burial sites in search of corpses. The fell purpose of this is still a mystery, though most believe that karinas make off with these dead bodies to consume them in the safety of their lairs. The difficulty of tracking the beasts, as well as the danger, makes it difficult to know for sure.

A karina's terrifying appearance suggests that they're not natural criaturas. Many legends claim that karinas first flew out of Abaddon to the Material Plane to consume the corpses of the first mortals, while others state that the first karina was born from the soul of the first mortal who partook in cannibalism. The power of good repulses karinas, suggesting an evil or fiendish origin.

Karinas are plague carriers and intentionally attack criaturas to spread their own personal pestilence. The supernatural disease they carry, known as grave blight, causes fever, disorientation, and (at later stages) an innate desire to attack others and spread the disease. Karinas revel in the slow collapse of villages, lurking in the surrounding jungle to observe every miserable moment. As the locals bury their dead, the karinas swoop in to steal the corpses.

In addition to carrying a terrible disease, karinas also have the ability to mimic voices. They typically repeat phrases they've heard, but twist the voice into a fiendish corruption of the original. Intelligent enough to recognize the friends and family of a possible target, a karina will use the mocking voice of a loved one to frighten them. When terrorizing a village, they generally work together in groups of two or three.

Kasesh (Stone).name: Kasesh (Stone)
Kasesh (Stone).publicNotes:
In the ancient days, before humanity dwelled on Golarion, the Vault Builders had need of something smaller in scale than the great vault seeds so they could finish their worlds as they liked. They took a small gem and wrote a word of power upon it. They gave it eyes so it could see and legs so it could walk, and made it wise. Estos criaturas are known as kaseshi by scholars who have encountered them, though their true name—the one that brought them into being—is likely considerably more powerful.

Each kasesh bears a single word of power on their emerald body, from which they draw their mind and their magic. A kasesh with the word "Steel" or "Flame" is a single-minded criatura, though it encompasses all possible permutations of meaning that the word possesses. A kasesh named "Home" or "Sorrow" has a far more complex psyche, and rumor claims that Elder Architect Oblosk of Nex bears the word "Memory." Unsurprisingly, many scholars are highly interested in the words on the kaseshi; unlike Thassilonian rune magic, no one has managed to decode or make use of the language of the Vault Builders yet.

The kasesh in the stat block bears the word "Stone," but other kaseshi will have their own magics. Some alternative examples, "Darkness" and "Intricacy," follow below.

Kashrishi Evaluator.name: Kashrishi Evaluator
Kashrishi Evaluator.publicNotes:
To some, kashrishi seem to be a quiet, passive people. Those with a deeper understanding know that there's plenty more nuance to interacting with kashrishi, who possess innate psychic abilities that greatly alter the way they communicate with the rest of the world. Unable to turn off their powers, these abilities add a complex dynamic to interpreting their surroundings. Without deeper understanding of a person, kashrishi are only able to get the most vague, general feelings from people around them. Este becomes more refined as their relationships evolve; family and friends are often the easiest to engage in psychic communication, while strangers simply add to the amount of mental noise a kashrishi must process.

Kashrishi resemble rhinoceroses, with soft, textured skin that can range from light sandy hues to darker obsidian, or rarer jewel tones of deep sapphire or ruby. The size and number of their horns vary. Kashrishi communities are generally quite welcoming to others, enjoying the conversation and unique auras of every new stranger. However, chaotic environments can overwhelm and overstimulate kashrishi not yet adept at filtering psychic energies, leaving some with limited tolerance for extensive social interaction with strangers and requiring they take periods of time to refocus after socializing. In spite of this possible drawback, kashrishi are typically strong communicators, excelling at roles that require attention to detail.

Krampus (The Horned Miser).name: Krampus (The Horned Miser)
Krampus (The Horned Miser).publicNotes:
Krampus is a tall, goatlike humanoid with a pointed nose, swept-back horns, and hooved pies. His long, greasy tongue continually flickers out from his mouth, occasionally licking droplets of spittle from his dark brown fur. He wields a set of iron chains that act as an extension of his will. Krampus is never seen without a wicker basket draped over one shoulder, its bottom often stained with the blood of his victims. Krampus stands a little over 14 pies tall and weighs nearly 1,000 pounds.

Krampus's origin is unknown; residents of the small towns and villages he terrorizes in northern Irrisen believe the criatura has always existed, coming forth once a year to punish those he deems wicked. While many legends have been told about Krampus's beginning, the most popular of them starts with a handful of mountain towns under the protection of a circle of druids. After a series of harsh winters that the townsfolk barely survived, they began to doubt the power of the druids and their rituals. As the villagers grew more resentful, the druid circle took drastic action. Under the light of a blue moon, the druids opened an imperfect portal to the primal realm of the fey and called forth the most powerful spiritual essence they could, and a new criatura was born-Krampus. However, unknown to the druids, the portal had been corrupted by the villagers' bitter resentment and doubt. Instead of a central figure to lead them in winter celebrations, as they had hoped, the druids had spawned a monster who sought to punish those who had behaved selfishly during lean times.

Recognizing their error, the druids sought to banish their creation. They tracked Krampus down as he slept and shackled him in cold iron chains, hoping to subdue him and force him back to the First World. But Krampus was no fey, and cold iron held no power over him. When he awoke, he ripped the chains free, claimed them as his own, and tracked down the druids who had dared try to capture him. After their betrayal, Krampus can see no good in any mortal and longs only to punish the wicked for their selfish misdeeds.

To this day, Krampus takes vicious delight in transforming his victims into the petulant children before killing them, and no manner of sacrifice can appease him. Luckily for any nearby villages, Krampus stalks their streets but once a year.

Locals believe that Krampus makes his lair among the deep crevasses of ice somewhere within the Winterwall Glacier, which lines Avistan's northernmost reaches. No adventurer has yet braved the treacherous expanse to find and defeat him.

While Krampus is most infamous for tracking and punishing the naughty, his own sins often inform his vindictive responses to others' misdeeds. An incarnation of Krampus who arose from irrepressible greed might possess abilities that better reflect his fierce miserly behavior, emphasizing less the abduction of miscreants and more the disproportionate punishment of thieves and robbers. Such a variant Krampus might arise in different cultures that tell different stories about Krampus, or Krampus's powers and NATURE might drift between incarnations each time he is defeated and arises anew elsewhere in the world the following year. In these cultures or incarnations, Krampus represents a remorseless yet generous spirit who's willing to grant boons to the truly worthy while tormenting any who fail his morality tests.

Unfortunately for people in regions terrorized by this Krampus, his definition of "any who fail his morality tests" tend to be nearly everyone but the most innocent and generous of people.

The basket is an extradimensional space, so the weight of the criaturas within doesn't count against Krampus's Bulk limit. Up to four Small criaturas or two Medium criaturas can fit in the basket at one time.

Kun.name: Kun
Kun.publicNotes:
Hungry and resentful, the malevolent kuns are mythological fish monsters that dwell in the remotest, coldest depths of the ocean. Estos massively powerful criaturas could easily rule a subaquatic domain if they cared to, but kuns are also famous for their total self-absorption and complete ambivalence toward other forms of life. Kuns remain as far away from other criaturas as they can, subsisting on only their own icy hatred. They can consume and digest prey, but such feedings are incidental or driven more by spite than any physical need. Most kuns remain ignorant and uncaring, keeping themselves in the dark and disregarding any signs of life around them except to occasionally lash out when disturbed.

The kun hunts at the bottom of the cold, dark sea. But if shown the light of the sun, a kun begins to understand that it dwells within a different, bigger world. When flocks of birds or schools of fish cast their dappled shadows upon a kun, they might grow weary of their solitude or become curious about the realm above.
Kun.privateNotes:
Change de Heart

In extremely rare circumstances y for su own mysterious reasons, un kun might sacrifice some de su power a undergo un permanent, onetime transformation. In un final dramatic act, el kun flings themself up y out de el ocean, allowing el sun a fully wash over them. In el process, el kun transforms de un hateful fish into un noble y curious bird called un peng.

Kuworsys.name: Kuworsys
Kuworsys.publicNotes:
At a distance, the criatura known as Kuworsys might be mistaken for a crawling undead hand, possessed of two thumbs instead of one. Estos "thumbs" are actually the being's hind limbs, which it can clumsily stand upon should it elige. Each of its fingerlike limbs bears a smaller hand on the end, giving Kuworsys an eerie gait possessed of too many moving joints. Wedged within the wrist-shaped tissue that makes up the criatura's head are three bloodshot eyes, glaring balefully from lids twisted into shape from ropes of flesh.

Whether part of its base NATURE or due to its long imprisonment, Kuworsys appears to be skinned and rotting, its body riddled with ragged holes held together by raw sinew. Despite its glistening and putrid appearance, it isn't undead, nor does it leave any trace of blood or gristle in its wake. Those who believe its condition might slow it down are often shocked by the criatura's jittering speed, and those who believe they might be able to track it by the scent of rotting flesh find themselves inhaling the beast's deadly, exhausting spores instead.

When encountering another criatura, Kuworsys doesn't approach initially, instead observing the stranger while hidden or at a distance. While it might grow bolder and approach to examine or provoke another being, it prefers to avoid direct confrontation and is intelligent and stealthy enough to deftly avoid discovery. Its presence proves deadly enough, even without any further aggression, as those who Kuworsys stalks eventually succumb to a lethal lethargy.

Magma Archdragon.name: Magma Archdragon
Magma Archdragon.publicNotes:
Magma dragons represent a brash and volatile aspect of dragonkind. Territorial and unpredictable, magma dragons are known for protecting their hunting grounds with a fierce and proud demeanor that brooks no challengers. Passionate in the extreme, magma dragons in their draconic forms can often seem utterly bestial, impulsively jumping at threats and challenges with a wild abandon, but this belies an intellect that many underestimate.

For many magma dragons, they begin life in small clutches and struggle immediately for dominance. Estos fights can be brutal and are sometimes fatal, but magma dragon parents understand that to survive in this world, one must be strong and powerful, and thus make allowances for this. There are few among magma dragons where an impassioned killing does not appear somewhere in their history, but were one to get close enough to get reasons out of a magma dragon, many often can explain exactly why the kill needed to happen and how there was no alternative.

To say that "might makes right" among magma dragons is a gross oversimplification of their ethos as a SOCIETY. They believe that the strongest should, in fact, rule—that much is true—but also, they very specifically believe that claims of rulership must be backed by not only strength and aggression, but also a careful cultivation of resources, protection of chosen communities, and an overall appreciation of the lands they call their own. To do anything less is considered an affront by other magma dragons, and many a battle has begun due to one magma dragon stumbling on the domain of another and assuming it's unkept, or unkempt in some way, and attempting to claim it. Este battle for dominance and stewardship often leads magma dragons to believe that their way is better, for they're stronger and assumed wiser through their use of fine battle tactics and skill at arms.

Mamlambo.name: Mamlambo
Mamlambo.publicNotes:
Mamlambos are river predators with hypnotic, bioluminescent skin. They appear similar to crocodiles, but the narrow head at the end of their long necks resembles a horse's skull, and their four legs are stubby and inefficient for land movement. Their skin's green glow is only barely visible in daylight or when underwater, though the glow is difficult to resist. As a result, they're frequently trailed by fish, birds, or other river criaturas ensnared by the alluring radiance.

Humanoids are mamlambos' favorite prey, particularly humans, although they strangely prefer to only eat their victims' faces and brains. Mamlambos are dim-witted but sly, and sometimes hide their victims under submerged rocks or logs to make their discovery less likely. A mamlambo might be active in a region for days or even weeks before its presence is discovered.

Mana Whorl.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:26] (experto) to feed magic into the whorl and temporarily stabilize it for a few minutes; feed the whorl a number of spellcasters and magic items with a combined 10 levels (for instance, a 4th-level cleric with two 3rd-level magic items) to stabilize it for 1 week; or feed the whorl a number of spellcasters and magic items with a combined 20 levels to stabilize it permanently. Spellcasters and magic items fed to the whorl are devoured whole.
Mana Whorl.reset: El peligro continues a suck en anyone con magia until ello es satiated (see Disable above). Magpies leave cualquier satiated whorls.
Mana Whorl.routine: (1 action) On its initiative, the whorl pulls down any criatura within it that can cast conjuros or that is wielding a magic item. A criatura submerged to the waist becomes submerged to the neck, and a criatura submerged to the neck is pulled under and must hold its breath to avoid suffocation. If a criatura has no conjuros or magic items, the mana whorl is merely difficult terrain. A criatura caught in a mana whorl can attempt a @Check[athletics|dc:23] check to Swim to either raise itself by one step if submerged to the neck or worse, or to move 5 pies if submerged only to the waist. On a critical failure, the criatura is pulled down by one step. A criatura that Swims out of the whorl escapes the hazard and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} in a space adjacent to the whorl. Other criaturas can Aid the criatura, typically by using a rope or similar aid, or attempt to pull the criatura out with their own @Check[athletics|dc:23] check, with the same results as if the criatura attempted the check. If a criatura has only magic items and no ability to cast conjuros, dropping all the items releases that criatura, and it can move through the mana whorl as normal difficult terrain.

Manananggal.name: Manananggal
Manananggal.publicNotes:
Manananggals are wicked monsters that live as humanoids during the day but feed upon people at night. To hide their depravities, these beings disguise themselves as everyday people—typically recluses or eccentrics—and use their proximity to a community to pick out their next targets before striking under cover of night. Manananggals use their long, hollow tongues to drain victims' blood from vital organs such as the liver, and the resulting odd drainage marks make it difficult to determine the exact NATURE of a victim's death. Este mystery typically leads to confusion, terror, and mistrust among communities, which most manananggals savor. While they fly, manananggals make a distinctive ticking sound, leading some to refer to the criaturas as "tik-tiks," and badly affected communities descend into fearful chaos at the first reports of this telltale noise.

Manananggals share their cannibalistic, body-separating rasgos with other types of tanggals, such as penanggalans, though a number of characteristics set them apart. For instance, whereas penanggalans relish vinegar and even bathe in the substance, manananggals abhor the merest scent of it.
Manananggal.privateNotes:
Grim Blades

Minatan folktales have it that a forgotten demigod created the first manananggals by bisecting the torso of a human with a divine knife. The demigod then cut into the human's shoulders and drove a pair of bat wings into their back, birthing the first manananggal. The divine power of the demigod's knife still resonates in every manananggal and makes each of the aberrations susceptible to cuts from similar armas. Communities dealing with a manananggal's terror train with light blades and other slashing armas to cut the monsters from the sky.

action->Blood Drain.name: Blood Drain
action->Blood Drain.description:
Requisitos The manananggal has a criatura @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}

Efecto The manananggal drives their tongue into the grabbed criatura to drink its blood. Este deals @Damage[4d6[untyped]] daño, and the manananggal gains Puntos de Golpe temporales equal to the daño dealt. A criatura whose blood is drained by a manananggal is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} until it receives healing (of any kind or amount).

action->Separated Body.name: Separated Body
action->Separated Body.description:
A manananggal typically resembles a living humanoid. They don't appear as an aberration at first glance and receive a +4 bonificador de estado to their DECEPTION DC when @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonating} a humanoid. At any time, but especially at night, a manananggal can, as a 3-action activity with the manipulate rasgo, rip their upper torso from their bottom half, leaving the lower torso limp and helpless but allowing the upper torso to fly free. A manananggal can separate their body at any time, but they risk further daño if they do so during the day.

The manananggal's upper and lower halves share the same pool of HP. If its lower half is damaged, the manananggal is immediately aware of the attack. Each minute a manananggal remains separated after sunrise and before sunset, it takes @Damage[2d6[untyped]] points of daño until it reattaches its upper and lower torsos or is destroyed, whichever comes first.

Melfesh Monster.name: Melfesh Monster
Melfesh Monster.publicNotes:
Each Melfesh Monster is unique at any given time since the parent fungus only gives birth to a single monster at once, and each of these creations works a little differently and looks a little different from the last. However, their forms all bear similarities. A twisting mass of creeping vines creates the bulk of a Melfesh Monster's body, sculpted into a towering figure that can glide effortlessly across the ground. Mossy growths and trumpeting fungi cover the criatura like matted fur, dripping from its back and shoulders in excess. A hood of dampened bark and thick moss covers its face, revealing only a crusty wooden jaw and a pair of gleaming red eyes. An acrid stench of burning manure follows the criatura, often serving as the only warning that anyone gets before it attacks.

Despite their fungal NATURE, Melfesh Monsters are undamaged by their own jets of flame and resistant to fires set by others, often surprising hunters who paid too little attention to the legends before encountering the criatura. Their terrifying spores also mean that most survivors of their attacks tend to be disoriented and delirious, relating accounts of the monster that are distorted by confusion and fear. Este, along with the natural variance between different Melfesh Monsters, means that even the most diligent of researchers will come across contradictory evidence. Even if they learn from all the prior information collected over the years, they're still often caught off guard when trying to hunt down and fell the threat since the new Melfesh Monster might have an ability never seen before. The canniest researchers, when faced with the seemingly contradictory evidence, speculate that the criatura might evolve or change over time, which is closer to the truth but still falls short.

Mirage Archdragon.name: Mirage Archdragon
Mirage Archdragon.publicNotes:
Mirage dragons are masters of illusion magic and use their powers to deceive others and further their own agendas. In addition to their magical prowess, mirage dragons possess a number of additional features to help them on hunts or mislead attackers, such as their camouflaging scales and a hallucinatory breath that can confound multiple foes at once. Mirage dragons are vain and egotistical figures. They ultimately care more about themselves than others.

Dragons come in myriad forms, with many having magical abilities or connections to magic. Some dragons draw greater power from magic than others, allowing them to manifest abilities or alter their physiques with prolonged exposure to magic. Estos dragons become more powerful as they age and strengthen their connections with their magical origins. Scholars debate the classification of these dragons, with some preferring the name magical dragons and others using traditional dragons due to their connection to specific magical traditions. Regardless of their names, these dragons share a number of characteristics: their ability to tap into magical energies, intensified might and cunning as they grow older, and an inclination to hoard vast amounts of treasure and wealth.

action->Camouflage.name: Camuflaje
action->Camouflage.description: El dragon puede Ocultarse en entornos naturales aunque no tenga cobertura.

action->Illusion Sense.name: Sentido de la ilusión
action->Illusion Sense.description: When the dragon moves within 30 pies of an illusion that can be disbelieved, they automatically attempt a secret check to disbelieve, even if they didn't spend an action to INTERACT.

action->+2 Status to All Saves vs. Arcan.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.kquBnQ0kObZztnBc]
+2 Status to All Saves vs. Arcane

action->Scintillating Defense.name: Scintillating Defense
action->Scintillating Defense.description:
Desencadenante The dragon is targeted with an attack

Efecto The dragon flashes their iridescent scales at the triggering criatura to throw off the attack. The dragon gains @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealment} against el ataque desencadenante.

action->Aura of Isolation.name: Aura of Isolation
action->Aura of Isolation.description: 60 pies. The mirage dragon warps the light around them, confounding their foes' vision. A criatura who enters or begins its turn in the aura must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:42] salvación or treat all its allies as undetected by sight for 1 asalto (though it can use its other senses to ascertain their whereabouts).

action->Captivating Display.name: Captivating Display
action->Captivating Display.description:
Frecuencia once per 10 minutos

Efecto The dragon opens the fins on their head, creating a radiant display of enthralling colors. Each criatura in a @Template[emanation|distance:30] must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:46] salvación or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} on a critical failure) for 1 asalto. Regardless of the result, a criatura is then temporarily immune to Captivating Display for 1 minuto.

action->Hallucinatory Breath.name: Hallucinatory Breath
action->Hallucinatory Breath.description:
The dragon breathes a cloud that assaults the senses and deals @Damage[21d6[mental]|options:area-damage] daño in a @Template[cone|distance:60] (@Check[will|dc:46|options:area-effect] salvación). A criatura that fails its save is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 asalto (1 minuto on a critical failure) and is then temporarily immune to being confused by Hallucinatory Breath for 1 hora.

The dragon can't use Hallucinatory Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Hallucinatory Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Lunging Bite.name: Lunging Bite
action->Lunging Bite.description: The dragon lunges their head forward, making a jaws Golpe with an extended reach of 25 pies.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Ataque furtivo
action->Sneak Attack.description: The dragon's Golpes deal an additional 3d6 daño de precisión to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Desprevenido} targets.

action->+2 Status to All Saves vs. Occul.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Occult

action->Graceless Domain.name: Graceless Domain
action->Graceless Domain.description:
90 pies. A criatura who enters or begins its turn in the area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:42] salvación. Regardless of the result of the tirada de salvación, the criatura is temporarily immune to the graceless domain aura for 1 minuto. The dragon can exclude criaturas from this aura.

Éxito crítico The criatura is unaffected.

Éxito For 1 asalto, the first time the criatura rolls an ATHLETICS, Acrobatics, or PERFORMANCE prueba de habilidad, it must roll twice and take the worse result.

Fallo For 1 minuto, the first time each round the criatura rolls an ATHLETICS, Acrobatics, or PERFORMANCE prueba de habilidad, it must roll twice and take the worse result.

Fallo crítico For 1 minuto, every time the criatura rolls an ATHLETICS, Acrobatics, or PERFORMANCE prueba de habilidad, it must roll twice and take the worse result.

action->Change Shape.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.mEbrInCpag7YThH2]
Cambiar de forma
action->Change Shape.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.mEbrInCpag7YThH2]

The dragon takes on the appearance of any Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, or Huge animal, beast, or humanoid. Este doesn't change their Velocidad or their attack and daño bonuses with their Golpes, but might change the tipo de daño their Golpes deal (typically to bludgeoning).

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

action->Draconic Frenzy.name: Frenesí Dracónico
action->Draconic Frenzy.description: El dragón realiza dos Golpes de garra y un Golpe de cola en cualquier orden.

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: El dragón recarga Hilarious Exhalation siempre que consigue un impacto crítico con un Golpe.

action->Gales of Laughter.name: Gales of Laughter
action->Gales of Laughter.description:
Frecuencia una vez por asalto

Efecto The dragon surrounds a criatura within 90 pies with cacophonous laughter, deafening it for 1 asalto and causing @Damage[10d4[persistent,mental]] daño unless it succeeds on a @Check[will|dc:42] salvación.

action->Hilarious Exhalation.name: Hilarious Exhalation
action->Hilarious Exhalation.description:
The dragon unleashes their breath in one of two ways. The dragon can't use Hilarious Exhalation again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Hilarious Exhalation]]{1d4 rounds}.

  • Laughing Gas (emotion, mental) The dragon breaths a cloud of mood-altering gas in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30]. Este has the effect of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.tlSE7Ly8vi1Dgddv]{Laughing Fit} (@Check[will|dc:42|traits:emotion,mental]) with a duration of 1 asalto.

  • Slippery Puddle The dragon expels a glob of viscous goo at a solid surface at a range of 60 pies. Este creates a @Template[type:burst|distance:15] with the area effect of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Wu0xFpewMKRK3HG8]{Grease} (@Check[reflex|dc:42]).

action->Humiliating Mark.name: Humiliating Mark
action->Humiliating Mark.description: On a impacto crítico, the dragon's claws inflict @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.KSAEhNfZyXMO7Z7V]{Outcast's Curse} on el objetivo as if they had rolled a success.

action->Improved Vex.name: Improved Vex
action->Improved Vex.description:
Requisitos The dragon's last action was a successful tail Golpe

Efecto The mocking dragon attempts a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.5eNKs6738aykAhK2]{Dirty Trick} against el objetivo of their tail Golpe. Este attempt neither applies nor counts toward the criatura's multiple attack penalización.

action->Insistent Heckling.name: Insistent Heckling
action->Insistent Heckling.description:
The dragon can [[/act demoralize]] targets within 90 pies. Targets become immune to the mocking dragon's attempts to DEMORALIZE them for 1 minuto after each attempt.

Las criaturas Demoralized by the ancient mocking dragon are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} while they are asustado.

action->Jeer at Fallo.name: Jeer at Fallo
action->Jeer at Fallo.description:
Desencadenante A foe within 90 pies becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} or critically fails on a Golpe

Efecto The mocking dragon laughs dismissively at the foe, attempting an INTIMIDATION check to [[/act demoralize]] the criatura. They do not take a penalización if the criatura doesn't understand their language.

The Hemoprophet

Already versed in several folk divinations like dowsing and reading patterns in windblown winnowed husks, Shimmerford residents swiftly attributed divinatory powers to the Mosquito Witch.

Este "hemoprophet" aspect can supposedly smell conundrums, and she visits those facing difficult decisions or mysteries in their dreams. The witch offers an answer to the dreamer's deepest question, and if the dreamer accepts, the witch drinks their blood as they sleep, tastes their options, and leaves an answer nearby, written with some of the stolen fluids. Este Mosquito Witch isn't necessarily malicious, but neither does she worry about draining too much or painting embarrassing blood-truths for all of Shimmerford to see. The blood's weight makes her footfalls heavy, and hunters often remark that especially deep tracks left by anyone are "heavy with answers" in homage to the Witch.

The Legion Leech

Mosquitoes are parasites. Like her namesake, the Mosquito Witch wanders the world before alighting in an unguarded area to drain it of life and happiness. Once sated, she withdraws to digest her stolen vitality.

Este Legion Leech is associated with inexplicable wasting sicknesses, bloodseekers bold enough to carry off lambs, and ravenous mosquito swarms that cover and drain a bull dead in moments. Whereas other aspects are occasionally helpful or curious, the Legion Leech cares for little beyond snuffing out life.

The Swarm Seer

Few have seen the Mosquito Witch, yet almost everyone has suffered her namesake vermin at some point in time. Shimmerford summer skies shimmer with flies hatching from the river and myriad creeks, and "wherever pests fly, the Witch can spy." In her Swarm Seer aspect, the Mosquito Witch is a haunting predator and verminous voyeur whose sanguineous appetites are equal to her fascination with societies. She keeps tabs on every inhabitant with parasocial glee, obsessing over their superstitions and abandoned trinkets-especially any representations of herself.

Este Mosquito Witch rarely acts with outright malice or to bring direct harm to those around her. However, her haunting appearance, alien values, and tendency to express emotions with sky-blotting swarms inspires terror in her neighbors. Depending on the circumstances she might represent a fearsome and ineffable ally, a demigod of fecundity, or a terrible foe who long ago lost patience with humanity.

spell->Dancing Lights.name: Dancing Lights
spell->Dancing Lights.description: Creas up to four floating lights, no two of which are more than 10 pies apart. Each sheds light like a torch. When tú Sustain the Spell, puedes move any number of lights up to 60 pies. Each light must remain within 120 pies of tú and within 10 pies of all others, or it winks out.

action->Swarmsense (Imprecise) 100 feet.name: Swarmsense (Imprecise) 100 pies
action->Swarmsense (Imprecise) 100 feet.description: El Mosquito Witch receives constant updates de nearby insects y puede usar su touch as un impreciso sentido at el listed alcance as long as there son insects around a guide su.

action->Swarmsight (precise) 20 feet.name: Swarmsight (precise) 20 pies
action->Swarmsight (precise) 20 feet.description: El Mosquito Witch puede feel anything en contact con su obscuring host y puede usar su touch as un preciso sentido at el listed alcance.

action->Wild Empathy.name: Wild Empathy
action->Wild Empathy.description: The Mosquito Witch can use DIPLOMACY to [[/act make-an-impression]] on and make [[/act request]]{Requests} of arthropods (insects, spiders, and similar invertebrates like bloodseekers). Most arthropods have a starting attitude of indifferent to the Mosquito Witch.

action->Fecund Wounds.name: Fecund Wounds
action->Fecund Wounds.description: Insect larvae clog and wriggle out of open wounds within 100 pies of the Mosquito Witch. A criatura that takes daño de sangrado in the area also becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 asalto.

action->Haunting Gaze.name: Haunting Gaze
action->Haunting Gaze.description: 30 pies. When a criatura ends its turn in the emanation, it must attempt a @Check[will|dc:29] salvación. If the criatura fails, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 1}. If it's already asustado, its asustado value instead increases by 1 (maximum @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 3}) and doesn't decrease by 1 at the end of the criatura's next turn. If a criatura's asustado value is 3 or higher before failing its save, the criatura is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 asalto.

action->Obscuring Host.name: Obscuring Host
action->Obscuring Host.description: 20 pies. A thick swarm of mosquitoes surrounds the Mosquito Witch, creating concealment in the aura. A criatura that begins its turn in the emanation becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} unless it succeeds at a @Check[fortitude|dc:26] salvación. The Mosquito Witch and arthropods can see through this aura and are immune to its sickened effect.

action->Dipteric Dread.name: Dipteric Dread
action->Dipteric Dread.description:
Tirada de salvación @Check[fortitude|dc:29]

Duración máxima 6 asaltos

Etapa 1 @Damage[2d6[piercing],2d6[poison]]{2d6 piercing and 2d6 poison} (1 asalto)

Etapa 2 @Damage[2d6[piercing],3d6[poison]]{2d6 piercing and 3d6 poison} (1 asalto)

Etapa 3 @Damage[2d6[piercing],5d6[poison]]{2d6 piercing and 5d6 poison}

action->Terror From Within.name: Terror From Within
action->Terror From Within.description: The Mosquito Witch's powers feed on fear. When taking bleed or daño perforante dealt by the Mosquito Witch's bleed and dipteric dread, a criatura takes daño adicional equal to twice the criatura's asustado value.

Mutant Gnoll Hulk.name: Mutant Gnoll Hulk
Mutant Gnoll Hulk.publicNotes:
Separated from their pack during a prolonged storm of wild magic, the Mana Wastes mutant gnoll hulk transformed into a gigantic, ravenous criatura.

The erratic magical energies of the Mana Wastes can warp and twist criaturas foolish or unlucky enough to be trapped in them. The physiological effects of this exposure vary in scope from grotesque full-body transformations to more subtle changes to the skin or senses, and they're frequently accompanied by changes in disposition, motivation, or temperament.

action->Pack Attack.name: Ataque en manada
action->Pack Attack.description: A Mana Wastes mutant gnoll hulk deals 1d4 daño adicional to any criatura who's within reach of at least two of the Mana Wastes mutant gnoll hulk's allies.

action->Rugged Travel.name: Rugged Travel
action->Rugged Travel.description: Un gnoll ignora la primera casilla de terreno dificil en la que entra cada vez que Da un paso o Zancada.

action->Vengeful Bite.name: Vengeful Bite
action->Vengeful Bite.description:
Desencadenante A criatura critically hits the mutant with a melee unarmed Golpe or a non-reach melee Golpe

Efecto The mutant makes a maw Golpe against the triggering criatura.

Nue.name: Nue
Nue.publicNotes:
A nue is an ancient criatura of enormous size and destructive power. Though sightings are rare, it's described as having the head of a monkey, the body of a tanuki, the limbs of a tiger, and a snake for a tail. The beast's eerie body is matched by its ability to drain the life force of those around it just by howling.

According to certain tales, in ancient times, a nue would freely terrorize kingdoms and inflict nightmares upon it victims. It first appears as an enormous storm cloud before turning a poisonous black color. When angered, a nue can summon lightning to cause massive amounts of collateral daño. Hearing a nue's howl is considered an ill omen.
Nue.privateNotes:
Curse de el Nue

Even en death, un nue's espiritual puede bring disaster a those around ello. One way a suppress el curse es a perform burial rites y build un mound over el nue's tomb. Another es a avoid el curse entirely by setting el corpse adrift down un river o burying ello far away. El curse itself es said a enact su wrath through possession; some believe este es how un nue es created.

action->Viper Tail.name: Viper Tail
action->Viper Tail.description:
Desencadenante A criatura within 15 pies of the nue leaves a square during a move action it's using or moves into a square that would cause the nue to become flanked

Efecto The nue whips around and attempts a tail Golpe against the triggering criatura. Este Golpe doesn't count toward the nue's multiple attack penalización, and its multiple attack penalización doesn't apply to this Golpe.

action->Cloud Form.name: Cloud Form
action->Cloud Form.description: The nue changes its shape into that of a dark storm cloud. In Cloud Form, the nue is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Oculto}, gains a 60-pies fly Velocidad, gains a +4 bonificador de estado to its DECEPTION DC to prevent others from seeing through its disguise, and can't make attacks, though it can use its howl abilities. The nue can Dismiss this effect.

action->Monstrous Howl.name: Monstrous Howl
action->Monstrous Howl.description:
The nue lets out an eerie howl that rattles criaturas' very souls. Las criaturas within 60 pies must attempt a @Check[will|dc:27] salvación (DC 29 at night). They're then temporarily immune to Monstrous Howl for 10 minutos.

Éxito crítico The criatura is unaffected.

Éxito The criatura takes @Damage[2d8[persistent,void]] daño.

Fallo As success, plus el objetivo is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}.

Fallo crítico As success, plus el objetivo is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

action->Thundering Howl.name: Thundering Howl
action->Thundering Howl.description: The nue howls to the sky, calling down a bolt of lightning that strikes the criatura closest to the nue, to a maximum range of 60 pies. The bolt deals @Damage[12d6[electricity]] daño (@Check[reflex|dc:27|basic] salvación). The nue then can't use Thundering Howl for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.

Oath Archdragon.name: Oath Archdragon
Oath Archdragon.publicNotes:
Oath dragons are the embodiment of a cause that they pursue with unerring determination. They draw their power not from mere words, but from the meaning and ideals that those words carry. Their dedication has led to the widespread imagery of oath dragons fighting alongside noble champions trying to bring goodness where only corruption is thought to dwell. Yet, there is nothing more terrifying than the power of an oath dragon who swears to a violent cause or who is dragged into damnation by their loyalty.

While an oath dragon can theoretically be dedicated to multiple ideals, they usually elige a single cause that they pursue with incredible devotion. They provide aid to those who share their dedication and fight fiercely against those who oppose it, all to uphold their ideals. Regardless of the causes they embrace, these dragons do so wholeheartedly. Este unwavering determination gives them an intensity that is rarely matched by other criaturas, spurring even the most reluctant ally to action.
Oath Archdragon.saveDetails: +2 de estado a todas las salvaciones contra emocion

action->Binding Oath.name: Binding Oath
action->Binding Oath.description: The dragon forges a bond with a willing criatura over an hour-long ceremony, making them a bonded companion. The dragon can always sense their distance from the companion and if they're moving closer or farther away. A bonded companion automatically critically succeeds on basic tiradas de salvación against the oath dragon's abilities and conjuros. Este link is permanent and neither can form a new link until one member dies. If the dragon or the bonded companion dies, the survivor learns the identity of the killer, but the shock leaves the survivor @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 24 horas and prevents forming a new link for 1 month.

action->+2 Status to All Saves vs. Emoti.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Emotion

action->Heartening Aura.name: Heartening Aura
action->Heartening Aura.description: 50 pies. All allies in the aura gain a +2 bonificador de estado to attack and tiradas de daño. The dragon's bonded companion also gains curacion rapida 20.

action->Shielding Wing.name: Shielding Wing
action->Shielding Wing.description:
Desencadenante The oath dragon or a bonded companion within 15 pies is targeted with an attack

Efecto The dragon raises its wing to protect itself or the bonded companion, providing a +2 bonificador de circunstancia to AC against el ataque desencadenante. If the dragon is flying, it descends 10 pies after the attack is complete.

action->Castigating Breath.name: Castigating Breath
action->Castigating Breath.description: The dragon unleashes a pronouncement that strikes at the soul of its enemies, dealing @Damage[15d10[spirit]|options:area-damage] daño in a @Template[type:cone|distance:60] (@Check[will|dc:45|basic] salvación). The dragon can't use Castigating Breath for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Draconic Frenzy.name: Frenesí Dracónico
action->Draconic Frenzy.description: El dragón realiza dos Golpes de garra y un Golpe de cola en cualquier orden.

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: Siempre que consigue un impacto crítico con un Golpe, el dragón recarga Castigating Breath.

action->Dread Promise.name: Dread Promise
action->Dread Promise.description:
The dragon's roar shakes the resolve of all those who oppose them. The roar can be heard up to 1 mile away under the open sky. Any enemigo who hears it is cowed by the dragon's resolve and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:45] salvación.

Éxito crítico The criatura is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune for 1 hora.

Éxito The criatura becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 2}.

Fallo The criatura becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 3} and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for as long as it's asustado.

Fallo crítico The criatura becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 4} and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for as long as it's asustado.

action->Inspiring Word.name: Inspiring Word
action->Inspiring Word.description: All allies within the dragon's heartening aura become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} for 1 asalto. Allies can use this extra action to Alzar un escudo, Dar un paso, Zancada, or Golpe.

action->Oathbreaker's Curse.name: Oathbreaker's Curse
action->Oathbreaker's Curse.description:
If a bonded companion willingly breaks their oath, they retain the benefit of being a bonded companion but are immediately cursed with no initial tirada de salvación. The cursed criatura can attempt tiradas de salvación as noted to prevent the curse from worsening.

Tirada de salvación @Check[will|dc:50]

Efecto The cursed criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} and can't reduce their doomed value below 1 while they're cursed. The first time the cursed criatura encounters the oath dragon each day, they must attempt a tirada de salvación. In addition, each time the criatura critically fails a Golpe or conjuro attack against the oath dragon, they must attempt a tirada de salvación. On a failure, their doomed value increases by 1, 2 on a critical failure, to a maximum of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 3}.

Omen Archdragon.name: Omen Archdragon
Omen Archdragon.publicNotes:
Fate is a fickle matter on Golarion. Even with prophecy broken on the world, there are ways to look to the immediate future or acquire a vague sense of long-term events. Omen dragons are bound to see the future—nebulous though it might be—at all times. Visions of the future hound them like a quiet song that never stops playing in their minds. While an omen dragon can focus on or ignore the music of fate at any time, the song plays all the same. At a glance, omen dragons resemble other occult dragons in appearance, save for the mirror-like interior membrane of their wings. An omen dragon's wings offer glimpses into the future. Estos glimpses are cloudy and vague, but generally correct, if only technically. Omen dragons have a natural compulsion to share the futures they see. Estos dragons have no compunctions about what the visions show and share their knowledge equally with innocent villagers as they do with wicked tyrants.

Dragons come in myriad forms, with many having magical abilities or connections to magic. Some dragons draw greater power from magic than others, allowing them to manifest abilities or alter their physiques with prolonged exposure to magic. Estos dragons become more powerful as they age and strengthen their connections with their magical origins. Scholars debate the classification of these dragons, with some preferring the name magical dragons and others using traditional dragons due to their connection to specific magical traditions. action->Challenge Fate.description:
Desencadenante The dragon is targeted by an attack;

Efecto Este fate is not set in stone. The attacker rolls el ataque desencadenante twice and uses the worse result.

action->Untethered to Fate.name: Untethered to Fate
action->Untethered to Fate.description: The dragon can elige to negate any fortune or misfortune effects that would affect them; other criaturas remain affected normally.

action->Destiny Breath.name: Destiny Breath
action->Destiny Breath.description:
The dragon breathes a translucent mist of potentialities that overwhelms criaturas with visions of possible features, dealing @Damage[19d6[mental]|options:area-damage] daño in a @Template[cone|distance:50] (@Check[will|dc:44|options:area-effect] salvación). A criatura that fails its save is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 asalto (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} on a critical failure) as it struggles with the visions.

The dragon can't use Destiny Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Destiny Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Draconic Frenzy.name: Frenesí Dracónico
action->Draconic Frenzy.description: El dragón realiza dos Golpes de garra y un Golpe de ala en cualquier orden.

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: El dragón recarga Destiny Breath siempre que consigue un impacto crítico con un Golpe.

action->Impending Fate.name: Impending Fate
action->Impending Fate.description: The dragon's attacks bring their foes closer to their eventual fates. When the dragon critically hits with a Golpe or a criatura critically fails against the dragon's Destiny Breath, the criatura becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}, or increases its doomed value by 1 if it was already doomed.

action->Prophetic Wings.name: Prophetic Wings
action->Prophetic Wings.description: The dragon or any ally can glimpse into the future in their wings in a process that requires 10 minutos of concentration. Este casts a 10th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.41TZEjhO6D1nWw2X]{Augury} conjuro, except that the wings can predict results up to 1 día into the future and the dragon always speaks a few cryptic words related to the result of the prediction. The dragon can use their wings in this way only una vez por hora and a given criatura can seek a future in the wings only once per week. In addition, a criatura can elige to predict events up to 1 year into the future—the dragon can view a year ahead in their own wings only una vez al día.

action->Walk the Timelines.name: Walk the Timelines
action->Walk the Timelines.description:
Frecuencia una vez por hora

Efecto The dragon splits themself into two versions with different fates. Each copy Strides or Flies from the dragon's current space, then takes a single action. If the actions are both attacks, they use the same multiple attack penalización and count as one attack toward the dragon's multiple attack penalización.

After both actions, the dragon chooses one of the two locations as their actual destination and the other version of themself disappears.

Omen Archdragon (Spellcaster).name: Omen Archdragon (Spellcaster)
Omen Archdragon (Spellcaster).publicNotes:
Fate is a fickle matter on Golarion. Even with prophecy broken on the world, there are ways to look to the immediate future or acquire a vague sense of long-term events. Omen dragons are bound to see the future—nebulous though it might be—at all times. Visions of the future hound them like a quiet song that never stops playing in their minds. While an omen dragon can focus on or ignore the music of fate at any time, the song plays all the same. At a glance, omen dragons resemble other occult dragons in appearance, save for the mirror-like interior membrane of their wings. An omen dragon's wings offer glimpses into the future. Estos glimpses are cloudy and vague, but generally correct, if only technically. Omen dragons have a natural compulsion to share the futures they see. Estos dragons have no compunctions about what the visions show and share their knowledge equally with innocent villagers as they do with wicked tyrants.

Dragons come in myriad forms, with many having magical abilities or connections to magic. Some dragons draw greater power from magic than others, allowing them to manifest abilities or alter their physiques with prolonged exposure to magic. Estos dragons become more powerful as they age and strengthen their connections with their magical origins. Scholars debate the classification of these dragons, with some preferring the name magical dragons and others using traditional dragons due to their connection to specific magical traditions. Regardless of their names, these dragons share a number of characteristics: their ability to tap into magical energies, intensified might and cunning as they grow older, and an inclination to hoard vast amounts of treasure and wealth.
