action->Ghostly Grasp.name: Agarre fantasmal
action->Ghostly Grasp.description: A shui gui can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.PMbdMWc2QroouFGD]{Grapple} corporeal criaturas despite being incorporeal. The shui gui uses its ATHLETICS check to Grapple as normal but can't use ATHLETICS for other actions that require corporeal contact, like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{FORCE OPEN} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trip}.

Sié Goluo.name: Sié Goluo
Sié Goluo.publicNotes:
Sié Goluo, sometimes referred to simply as Grandfather, is an ancient spirit that has kept watch over the peoples of the Mwangi Expanse for generations. Most believe he first appeared during the Age of Darkness to protect the Mwangi people from the worst dangers of the everlasting night. Bekyar storytellers claim he is older still, from a time before the first people walked Golarion. Este immortal spirit has incarnated into multiple forms over millennia. In the oldest surviving tales, they say Sié Goluo looked like an ordinary-if oversized-ox, save for his nearly human-looking eyes. Most recently, people say he has the appearance of several different animals, but accounts vary on which animals make up his form.

When a traveling farmer is assailed by a deadly beast, or a small village faces the wrath of an advancing army, Sié Goluo manifests in whatever form will allow him to best defend them. There seem to be no geographical limitations on where he can manifest, as there are tales of him saving Mwangi adventurers as far spread as Tian Xia and Arcadia.

spell->Humanoid Form (At Will).name:

Forma humanoide (a voluntad)

Pass Without Trace (Constant)

action->Spirit Steps.name: Spirit Steps
action->Spirit Steps.description: Sie Goluo ignora el terreno dificil y no desencadena trampas con su movimiento.

action->Ancestral Response.name: Ancestral Response
action->Ancestral Response.description:
Desencadenante A criatura on the Material Plane calls out for Sié Goluo

Efecto Sié Goluo instantaneously appears in an unoccupied space within 30 pies of the triggering criatura and heals @Damage[8d8[healing]] Puntos de Golpe on all allies that can see him within 60 pies. Allies healed this way gain a +2 bonificador de circunstancia on tiradas de salvación for 1 minuto.

Las criaturas that receive these benefits become temporarily immune to them for 1 year.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.gxBjyPaYDdhjAImf]{Efecto: Ancestral Response}

action->Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenecimiento
action->Rejuvenation.description: Cuando Sié Goluo es destruido, el reforms, fully healed, at un location de su choosing anywhere en el Material Plane after [[/br 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days}. Si every person de Mwangi descent rejects belief en Sié Goluo, el espiritual es permanently destruido.

action->Spirit Charge.name: Spirit Charge
action->Spirit Charge.description:
Sié Goluo Strides twice, then makes a horn Golpe. On a hit, Sié Goluo creates a shock wave that deals @Damage[4d12[force]|options:area-damage] daño in a @Template[cone|distance:30] (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect,forced-movement] salvación).

Las criaturas that fail their save are pushed away 5 pies (10 pies on a critical failure).

Skinskitter.name: Skinskitter
Skinskitter.publicNotes:
Estos elusive oddments resemble discarded hides of butchered animals and fleshwarping experiments, floating like so much meaty detritus in the bloody filth of Ecanus's charnel-clogged sewers. Skinskitters, named for their fluid, erratic movements, scavenge the city for leavings of fleshy waste. They prefer discreet, non-violent ways of procuring these biological materials and shy from combat, seemingly possessed of a nervous temperament. Nexian fleshforgers quip this is entirely reasonable, as skinskitters are little more than nervous systems wrapped in dying skin. Nexian guards who actually have to hunt these fleshforged pests aren't quite as jocular; confronted by the oddly childlike pleas of these cornered puddles of flesh, hair, and eyes, many recruits simply elige to leave the city watch.

On occasion, curious scholars or soldiers have questioned why skinskitters pursue organic tissue, and whether this is a simple instinct or in pursuit of a grander purpose. Most fleshforgers assume that skinskitters consume organic matter to REPAIR themselves in a process similar to eating, and give the matter no further thought, showing no more interest in the criaturas than a smith might show in a bead of melted slag. The most paranoid Nexians claim that skinskitters are attempting to build something out of their collections of cast-off skin, perhaps even reconstructing themselves into fleshforged conformers. There is no recorded evidence of this ever occurring, however—if the criaturas have any awareness at all, it's more likely that skinskitters are driven by the basest of instincts to better themselves through the same methods used in their creation but lack the understanding and self-direction to ever succeed.

action->A Taste for Skin.name: A Taste for Skin
action->A Taste for Skin.description: A skinskitter tastes skin (including leather), hair, claws, and nails within 60 pies.

action->Shuddering Skitter.name: Shuddering Skitter
action->Shuddering Skitter.description:
Frecuencia una vez al día

Desencadenante The skinskitter is reduced to 0 HP

Efecto The fear of death agitates the skinskitter, precipitating a sudden existential awakening of consciousness. The skinskitter is reduced to 1 HP, loses the mindless rasgo and immunity to mental effects for the next 24 horas, gains the ability to speak one language (typically Osiriani or Vudrani), and takes two of the following actions in any order: Hide, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.VMozDqMMuK5kpoX4]{Sneak}, Dar un paso, Zancada, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ust1jJSCZQUhBZIz]{Take Cover}. In addition, the square occupied by the skinskitter before using Shuddering Skitter becomes difficult terrain, as they disgorge a shower of half-digested calluses, chewed nails, and entangled hair in their skittering wake.

action->Share the Skin.name: Share the Skin
action->Share the Skin.description:
Requisitos A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}, or willing criatura is within the skinskitter's reach

Efecto The skinskitter scrapes and shears away large sheets of the victim's skin. Este requires an @Check[athletics|defense:fortitude] check against the victim's Fortitude DC if the victim is grabbed and is automatic for any of the other conditions. The massive pain causes the victim to become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 minuto, and the skinskitter drapes itself in the flapping skin, granting it 10 Puntos de Golpe temporales for 1 minuto.

Sky Archdragon.name: Sky Archdragon
Sky Archdragon.publicNotes:
When the imperial dragons first arrived in the Universe, each was well-attuned to the elemental planes they hailed from. As the war between the Elemental Lords raged on and the benevolent lords fell one by one, the Planes of Metal and Wood sealed themselves away. For the dragons who originated from the Corroded Core, their very existence was now at stake. Estos dragons flew from mountaintop to mountaintop, seeking refuge from the then-perilous Tian Xia overrun by warring yaoguai. Finally, upon the mountain peaks of Chenlun, Gossamer, Kelsang, Kimu, Kullan, Kyojin, and the Wall of Heaven, celestial beings answered the dragons' cries for help. What the dragons no longer had in elemental metal, these celestials provided through divine blessings and essence. With their NATURE changed, the dragons as a species survived. In time, their proximity to the sky and the deities they serve became their namesake. Their past as elemental metal dragons became but a faded memory and creation myth for all but the sky dragons themselves to remember.

The sky dragons proved their gratitude with eternal service. Some became infused with the planar energies of the gods they served, becoming massive and powerful; many were among the progenitors of the modern empyreal dragon. Others stayed in the Universe, practicing their faith and perfecting the divine arts over life and spirit. Rare indeed are sky dragons who strike out on their own, wielding non-divine powers on missions unrelated to a greater will. The few who do retain much of their reclusive and contemplative NATURE, at least during their younger years.

With the recent return of the Plane of Metal, there have been careful inquiries about sky dragons' connection to that plane. Some wonder if they might find surviving distant relations. Estos inquiries are not out of curiosity, but need. While being empowered by celestial beings gave the sky dragons the power to defend themselves, it didn't solve the issue of elemental deficiency. Worse, the deficiency continues despite the Corroded Core's return. Sky dragon hatchlings, from eggs or live birth, are born vulnerable, with only patches of scales or none at all. Even with exposure to large deposits of mineral or salt veins (which serve as magnets and reservoirs for elemental metal energy), it can take decades before a hatchling's scales toughen to the point that they have adequate protection to leave the lair. If the Plane of Metal has an answer to this issue—either locations that might serve as a safe birthing or hatching grounds or a way to restore the dragon's ability to absorb ambient elemental energy—it's of utmost importance that all sky dragons learn of the method and opportunity.

action->Mist Vision.description: Fog and mist don't impair a sky dragon's vision; they ignore the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Oculto} condition from fog and mist.

+2 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

action->Countered by Fire.description:
If the sky dragon takes daño de fuego, the elemental magic of metal within them is tempered. Until the end of their next turn, they take a –1 penalización de circunstancia to tiradas de ataque and AC, and their jaws Golpes don't deal daño de electricidad. Este limitation ends if the dragon uses Steel Lightning Breath.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.a4bZrBNL17zPjDiH]{Efecto: Countered by Fire}

action->Fed by Earth.name: Fed by Earth
action->Fed by Earth.description: When a sky dragon is targeted by an earth conjuro or effect, they crystallize the minerals in their scales to create a light-bending or light-scattering layer for camouflage. For 1 minuto, the dragon is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Oculto} while flying.

action->Frightful Presence.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.etMnv73EIdEZrYYu]

90 pies @Check[will|dc:42]

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.FrightfulPresence]

action->Coiling Frenzy.description: The dragon makes one claw Golpe and one tail Golpe in either order, each against the same target. If either Golpe hits, the dragon can attempt to GRAB el objetivo with that limb as a free action. The dragon can have up to three criaturas @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} at a time; one in each of its front claws, and a last with their tail.

action->Divine Lightning.description:
Requisitos The dragon worships a deity whose sanctification entry lists "holy"

Efecto The sky dragon channels divine power through its attacks, making them more effective against the unholy. Any daño de electricidad it deals becomes daño de espíritu against unholy criaturas.

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: The dragon recharges Steel Lightning Breath siempre que they score a impacto crítico with a Golpe.

action->Greater Constrict.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.OmV6E3aELvq9CkK1]

@Damage[(4d10+10)[bludgeoning]], @Check[fortitude|dc:44|basic]

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.GreaterConstrict]

action->Metallic Strikes.description: The sky archdragon's jaws and claw Golpes counts as any metal for the purposes of calculating immunities, resistances, and weaknesses. Perfected Flight As young sky dragon.

action->Perfected Flight.name: Perfected Flight
action->Perfected Flight.description: Un sky dragon puede hover en place sin spending un action, y ellos automatically succeed at todos Acrobatics pruebas a Maneuver en Flight.

action->Steel Lightning Breath.description: The dragon shoots a ball of electricity that deals @Damage[12d12[electricity]|options:area-damage] daño in a @Template[type:burst|distance:40] within 75 pies (@Check[reflex|dc:44|basic] salvación). They can't use Steel Lightning Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Steel Lightning Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Stunning Electricity.name: Stunning Electricity
action->Stunning Electricity.description:
The dragon rapidly coils, then unleashes crackling lightning that deals @Damage[5d12[electricity]|options:area-damage] daño in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:60]. Each criatura in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:44] salvación; regardless of the outcome, the criatura then becomes temporarily immune for 10 minutos.

Éxito crítico The criatura is unaffected.

Éxito The criatura takes half daño and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Fallo The criatura takes full daño, is aturdido for 1 asalto, and can't fly for 4 asaltos.

Fallo crítico The criatura takes double daño, is aturdido for 2 asaltos, and can't fly for 1 minuto.

Sky Dragon (Young, Spellcaster).name: Sky Dragon (Young, Spellcaster)
Sky Dragon (Young, Spellcaster).publicNotes:
When the imperial dragons first arrived in the Universe, each was well-attuned to the elemental planes they hailed from. As the war between the Elemental Lords raged on and the benevolent lords fell one by one, the Planes of Metal and Wood sealed themselves away. For the dragons who originated from the Corroded Core, their very existence was now at stake. Estos dragons flew from mountaintop to mountaintop, seeking refuge from the then-perilous Tian Xia overrun by warring yaoguai. Finally, upon the mountain peaks of Chenlun, Gossamer, Kelsang, Kimu, Kullan, Kyojin, and the Wall of Heaven, celestial beings answered the dragons' cries for help. What the dragons no longer had in elemental metal, these celestials provided through divine blessings and essence. With their NATURE changed, the dragons as a species survived. In time, their proximity to the sky and the deities they serve became their namesake. Their past as elemental metal dragons became but a faded memory and creation myth for all but the sky dragons themselves to remember.

The sky dragons proved their gratitude with eternal service. Some became infused with the planar energies of the gods they served, becoming massive and powerful; many were among the progenitors of the modern empyreal dragon. Others stayed in the Universe, practicing their faith and perfecting the divine arts over life and spirit. Rare indeed are sky dragons who strike out on their own, wielding non-divine powers on missions unrelated to a greater will. The few who do retain much of their reclusive and contemplative NATURE, at least during their younger years.

With the recent return of the Plane of Metal, there have been careful inquiries about sky dragons' connection to that plane. Some wonder if they might find surviving distant relations. Estos inquiries are not out of curiosity, but need. While being empowered by celestial beings gave the sky dragons the power to defend themselves, it didn't solve the issue of elemental deficiency. Worse, the deficiency continues despite the Corroded Core's return. Sky dragon hatchlings, from eggs or live birth, are born vulnerable, with only patches of scales or none at all. Even with exposure to large deposits of mineral or salt veins (which serve as magnets and reservoirs for elemental metal energy), it can take decades before a hatchling's scales toughen to the point that they have adequate protection to leave the lair. If the Plane of Metal has an answer to this issue—either locations that might serve as a safe birthing or hatching grounds or a way to restore the dragon's ability to absorb ambient elemental energy—it's of utmost importance that all sky dragons learn of the method and opportunity.

Solar Ibis.name: Ibis Solar
Solar Ibis.publicNotes:
Solar ibis are beings of light sometimes called sun birds, or "winged luminaries" by the more scholarly inclined. They're tasked with guarding sacred places or items, although they sometimes also protect the living from places of incredible danger. Their appearance is always preceded by numerous small purple-winged birds with a splash of yellow on their crowns; these are avatars of the ibis that nest and congregate in areas it protects. The presence of these avatars is often the only way to track these reclusive and solitary criaturas. Should the solar ibis elige to appear, these little birds scatter like wild fowl. The sun bird then manifests and bathes the area in a brilliant shower of light that can blind and startle unwary and unprepared criaturas in its presence.

The solar ibis appears as a magnificent, large bird surrounded by a halo of brilliant light. Its black feathers shimmer with all the colors of the spectrum, casting glossy rainbows across its plumage. It has a keen sense of insight, which it uses to pass judgment as a whole on whether those before it are worthy to access what it guards. It punishes those it finds unworthy with its cleansing might.

Though considered sacred by most within the Mwangi Expanse, there are still some who hunt these glorious criaturas; some seek the treasures that the ibis keep, while others seek the ibis themselves, dead or alive. Some believe that the feathers of a solar ibis, when burned, create an incense that can grant holy power to those that inhale it. Others believe that its bones and pies can be ground into a powder that can destroy demons and purify the undead.

Sovereign Archdragon.name: Sovereign Archdragon
Sovereign Archdragon.publicNotes:
There were supposedly dragons of pure elemental earth, once. Estos were imperial dragons who, like their other elemental counterparts, came to the Universe, lived, and died, their bodies becoming part of the continent. As fire became lava, wood became forests, water the seas, lakes, and rivers, and metal the veins of precious minerals, so earth became the land, the stone, the mountains. By way of logic, if there exist such environments and entities today, then earth dragons must exist too. Or have existed, once upon a primeval time.

And yet among the imperial dragons today there are only sovereign dragons, who leave serpentine skeletons behind upon death in place of rock, stone, or land. The dragons' innate spellcasting, weakness to unheated iron, and other rasgos highly suggest that they're associated with elemental earth. The rest of their powers have little to no such association, instead centered on the mysteries of the metaphysical spirit and mind.

There's no clear explanation for why sovereign dragons are the way they are today. Some guess it might have been a deal to fulfill personal ambition, to go from those tasked with selecting rulers to becoming the rulers themselves. Others wonder if the lands of Tian Xia were corrupted in the past, and the earth dragons walked away from their elemental natures to save themselves. Perhaps they too became empyreal dragons, but then returned to the lands of mortals when no suitable ruler rose to the throne.

spell->Wish (doesn't require secondary c.description:
Tú weave the fabric of reality itself to grant el objetivo's greatest desire. El objetivo declares their wish in a loud voice at the start of the ritual and again at the end. El objetivo's wish can be anything, ranging from simpler wishes such as vast riches or the casting of a certain conjuro or ritual, to greater wishes like the destruction of an entire kingdom or ascension to divinity. The GM might decide a wish draws the attention of deities or other powerful criaturas, leading to interference with the ritual or attempts to undo the wish. The power of the ritual alters reality to such a degree that even deities can't outright undo the wish, but they can react to the wish by sending servitors to take away the newly acquired riches, for example.

Éxito crítico The wish is granted without complication or drawbacks.

Éxito The wish is granted, but with unintended consequences or side effects, such as taking riches from a well-known criminal, stirring a damaged kingdom to war, or angering rival gods.

Fallo The wish fails and has no result. The GM can instead have the wish be partially granted, but to such a lesser degree that el objetivo will be eternally unsatisfied.

Fallo crítico The wish is corrupted, resulting in a cruel fulfillment. The GM determines the full results, but the outcome is generally ironic in some NATURE, such as becoming trapped in an underground vault full of riches, being transported to the kingdom as it's destroyed, or achieving divinity within an inaccessible demiplane.

Sovereign Dragon (Adult).name: Sovereign Dragon (Adult)
Sovereign Dragon (Adult).publicNotes:
There were supposedly dragons of pure elemental earth, once. Estos were imperial dragons who, like their other elemental counterparts, came to the Universe, lived, and died, their bodies becoming part of the continent. As fire became lava, wood became forests, water the seas, lakes, and rivers, and metal the veins of precious minerals, so earth became the land, the stone, the mountains. By way of logic, if there exist such environments and entities today, then earth dragons must exist too. Or have existed, once upon a primeval time.

And yet among the imperial dragons today there are only sovereign dragons, who leave serpentine skeletons behind upon death in place of rock, stone, or land. The dragons' innate spellcasting, weakness to unheated iron, and other rasgos highly suggest that they're associated with elemental earth. The rest of their powers have little to no such association, instead centered on the mysteries of the metaphysical spirit and mind.

There's no clear explanation for why sovereign dragons are the way they are today. Some guess it might have been a deal to fulfill personal ambition, to go from those tasked with selecting rulers to becoming the rulers themselves. Others wonder if the lands of Tian Xia were corrupted in the past, and the earth dragons walked away from their elemental natures to save themselves. Perhaps they too became empyreal dragons, but then returned to the lands of mortals when no suitable ruler rose to the throne.

Sovereign Dragon (Young, Spellcaster).name: Sovereign Dragon (Young, Spellcaster)
Sovereign Dragon (Young, Spellcaster).publicNotes:
There were supposedly dragons of pure elemental earth, once. Estos were imperial dragons who, like their other elemental counterparts, came to the Universe, lived, and died, their bodies becoming part of the continent. As fire became lava, wood became forests, water the seas, lakes, and rivers, and metal the veins of precious minerals, so earth became the land, the stone, the mountains. By way of logic, if there exist such environments and entities today, then earth dragons must exist too. Or have existed, once upon a primeval time.

And yet among the imperial dragons today there are only sovereign dragons, who leave serpentine skeletons behind upon death in place of rock, stone, or land. The dragons' innate spellcasting, weakness to unheated iron, and other rasgos highly suggest that they're associated with elemental earth. The rest of their powers have little to no such association, instead centered on the mysteries of the metaphysical spirit and mind.

There's no clear explanation for why sovereign dragons are the way they are today. Some guess it might have been a deal to fulfill personal ambition, to go from those tasked with selecting rulers to becoming the rulers themselves. Others wonder if the lands of Tian Xia were corrupted in the past, and the earth dragons walked away from their elemental natures to save themselves. Perhaps they too became empyreal dragons, but then returned to the lands of mortals when no suitable ruler rose to the throne.

Spellscar Fext.name: Spellscar Fext
Spellscar Fext.publicNotes:
Spellscar fexts are spellcasters who were destroyed by wild magic or wellspring surges they tried—and failed—to control. The magical feedback that snuffed out their life warped and animated their flesh, twisting them into shambling undead. Spellscar fexts stand 6 pies tall with disproportionately long arms that end in clusters of waving magical tendrils.

Almost all who became spellscar fexts entered the Mana Wastes to harness the power of the area's wild magic. Once transformed, the desire for magical power becomes a spellscar fext's singular motivation. The criaturas focus their attacks on magic users they encounter, attempting to kill them and strip their magic. Unfortunately for a spellscar fext, their transformation makes their entire being inimical to magic. They're unable to cast even the simplest of conjuros. They grasp destructively at magic they can never hold.

Difficult for the unprepared to destroy permanently, spellscar fexts harry trade routes known for shipping magical goods and repeatedly attack arcane workshops on the borders of the Mana Wastes. They're particularly dangerous to spellcasters traveling alone, as battling the criaturas might trigger a wellspring surge that could destroy the lone magic user.

As the fext's vulnerability to glass armas has become more well known, enterprising gunsmiths in Alkenstar have begun CRAFTING glass ammunition, an uncommon item that costs the same as cold iron ammunition.

Spring-Heeled Jack.name: Spring-Heeled Jack
Spring-Heeled Jack.publicNotes:
The greatest secret of the murderous trickster known as Spring-Heeled Jack is that he isn't a unique criatura. Instead, he's one of a rare type of fey native to the First World who enjoy causing bloody mayhem in the Material Plane. Estos fey are so rare and so distrustful of one another's company that two have never been seen together; the mistaken assumption that only a single Spring-Heeled Jack exists is therefore entirely understandable. The fact that sightings occur across Ustalav (and beyond) and across centuries of time is ascribed to the trickster's long lifespan and mysterious ability to travel quickly, or to the belief that there's no such criatura, merely an urban legend that twisted minds attempt to bring to life through costumes, magic, and a series of murders and mayhem. Even in fear-drenched Ustalav, no one has yet guessed that multiple Spring-Heeled Jacks exist or postulated that some future event might drive them to overcome their mutual disdain and gather into a murderous cabal, far more powerful than the sum of its parts.

Spring-Heeled Jacks are cruel-eyed, hairy fey with vaguely humanoid shapes and extra features that cause them to be easily mistaken for demons or devils. Glowing eyes, cloven hooves, menacing horns, and a pointed tail combine to create the mien of a wicked imp; his love of sudden and sadistic violence completes the impression. Almost all have jet-black skin and fur, though a few exceptions might exist.

Spring-Heeled Jacks typically hide their features in tattered cloaks, appearing as a hunched elder or a youth in the nighttime conditions they enjoy. Such a disguise rarely holds up to any scrutiny, but that doesn't matter much to the Spring-Heeled Jack, who only needs something that offers just enough doubt for their target to move within striking distance, which can be from much farther away than most other criaturas even realize. Once close enough, the Spring-Heeled Jack leaps startling distances in the blink of an eye to easily slash at a victim who had, until that moment, considered themself safe.

Stone Sister.hpDetails: curación de vacío, reconstitution, stone flesh
Stone Sister.publicNotes:
Stone sisters are the tragic undead remains of an ancient Holoma army, petrified en masse by the necromancer Geb. The armies of Holomog were once a dominant force in the region, repelling several invasions from powerful rivals. However, when they sought to expand into the nation of Geb, their campaign quickly ended. Shortly after crossing Geb's southern border, the entire army was struck by a terrible curse that turned every warrior into a stone statue. Now known as the Field of Maidens, the statues have stood frozen for centuries, armas in hand.

Yet some of these warriors possess a will even stronger than stone. When approached, there's a chance the spirits of the fallen will animate their statues and attack outsiders with the same deadly coordination they had in life.

action->Reconstitution.name: Reconstitution
action->Reconstitution.description: Until Geb's curse is broken, any stone sister who's destroyed gradually reforms in her original shape. A stone sister who's reduced to 0 Puntos de Golpe will reform after 24 horas, while one reduced to rubble or dust might take a year or more to reform. Stone sisters who are removed from the Field of Maidens always attempt to return to it when they reconstitute.

action->Stone Flesh.name: Stone Flesh
action->Stone Flesh.description:
A stone sister is made of a bizarre stone that never stops bleeding from numerous cracks along her skin. She reacts to certain conjuros in unique ways, as listed below.

  • Spells that alter earth, such as shape stone, either deal @Damage[3d10] points of daño or heal @Damage[3d10[healing]] Puntos de Golpe, as decided by the caster. If the conjuro is specifically harmful or beneficial to earth and stone, the GM might decide it can only harm the stone sister, or only heal her.
  • Stone to flesh doesn't revert a stone sister to flesh and blood but instead weakens her. She loses her resistance to daño físico for 1 minuto. If she's reduced to 0 Puntos de Golpe during this time, she's permanently destroyed and can't reform.

action->Curse of Stone.name: Curse of Stone
action->Curse of Stone.description:
The criatura must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:21] salvación or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 3} on a critical failure) and gain a +1 bonificador de estado to AC as their skin hardens to stone. The torpe condition can be temporarily relieved for 24 horas by casting stone to flesh on the cursed criatura but can't be removed or reduced by any other means short of removing the curse; during this time, the cursed criatura also no longer receives the bonificador de estado to AC.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.UgoM6FBiZfc7KqCV]{Efecto: Curse of Stone}

action->Statue.name: Estatua
action->Statue.description: Until the next time she acts, the stone sister appears to be a statue. She has an automatic result of 34 on DECEPTION checks and DCs to pass as a statue. Since the Field of Maidens is filled with thousands of statues just like her, most of which aren't stone sisters, it's incredibly difficult to recognize her true NATURE.

Storm Discharge.description: Ebeshra aligns su crystalline form a produce un blast de lightning que charges el surrounding area con electrical energy.

Storm Discharge.reset: Ebeshra espera [[/gmr 1d4 #Espera de estallido electrico]] asaltos antes de otro estallido.

action->Lightning Blast.name: Lightning Blast
action->Lightning Blast.description:
Desencadenante A criatura takes a hostile action against Ebeshra, produces a visible area effect, or flies within 120 pies of Ebeshra

Efecto Ebeshra unleashes a @Template[line|distance:240] of electricity toward the triggering criatura. Las criaturas in the line take @Damage[16d8[electricity]|options:area-damage] daño (@Check[reflex|dc:42|basic|options:area-effect] salvación). The electricity creates a static field in all squares that the line passed through and all adjacent squares. For 1 asalto, any criaturas that enter a space in the static field take @Damage[4d8[electricity]|options:area-damage] daño (@Check[reflex|dc:38|basic|name:Static Field|options:area-effect] salvación).

Stormcrown Archdragon.name: Stormcrown Archdragon
Stormcrown Archdragon.publicNotes:
Heralds of—and heralded by—the primal forces of thunder and lightning, stormcrown dragons meld the majesty of fierce storms and mighty dragons. Driven by emotion and curiosity, these mercurial dragons can change from friend to foe or threatening to thoughtful in mere moments.

While no strangers to the personality rasgos for which dragons are well-known—pride, imperiousness, desire for lovely things, and so on—stormcrown dragons are by NATURE gregarious, even jovial. Indeed, these dragons often mingle with local communities or extend invitations for everything from raucous feasts to elegant soirees. To offend a stormcrown dragon, however, is most unwise. Insults to the dragon's hospitality or friendship, assertions of authority, and demands on them are all likely to elicit a tempestuous response, in every sense of the word. Cursed metamorphosis is a personal favorite of older stormcrown dragons for the disrespectful and demanding, forcing shapes on them more befitting their insignificance. A stormcrown dragon's fury often passes as suddenly as it arises, however, particularly when dulled by a suitable display of contrition.

action->Frightful Presence.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.etMnv73EIdEZrYYu]

100 pies @Check[will|dc:37]

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.FrightfulPresence]

action->Superconductor.name: Superconductor
action->Superconductor.description:
Desencadenante The dragon is targeted by an attack or conjuro

Efecto The dragon uses the displaced air or magical trajectory of the attack as a channel for its electrical energy. The dragon attempts a storm bolt Golpe against the attacker, regardless of range.

action->Command Lightning.name: comando Lightning
action->Command Lightning.description:
Requisitos The dragon's last action was to use Draconic Frenzy or Lanzar un conjuro with the air or electricity rasgo and they're in an area of stormy weather

Efecto The dragon directs a bolt of lightning at a criatura within 100 pies, dealing @Damage[5d12[electricity]] daño with a @Check[reflex|dc:44|basic] salvación.

action->Coronal Cloak.name: Coronal Cloak
action->Coronal Cloak.description: When the dragon spends an action to Hover while in stormy weather, they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Oculto} until they move or until the beginning of their next turn, whichever comes first.

action->Draconic Frenzy.name: Frenesí Dracónico
action->Draconic Frenzy.description: El dragón realiza dos Golpes de garra y un Golpe de cola en cualquier orden.

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: The dragon recharges Galvanic Barrage siempre que they score a impacto crítico with a Golpe.

action->Furious Cloudburst.name: Furious Cloudburst
action->Furious Cloudburst.description:
Frecuencia una vez al día

Requisitos The dragon must be outdoors and aboveground

Efecto The dragon exhales a massive bolt of lightning directly upward to create a terrible storm centered on the dragon. Strong winds blow in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:120] that lasts for 10 minutos; this creates greater difficult terrain for both flying criaturas and criaturas on the ground. Las criaturas in the area except for the dragon take a –2 penalización de circunstancia to Acrobatics and Perception checks and a –4 penalización de circunstancia to ranged attacks due to the wind and rain. Este counts as stormy weather for the dragon's comando Lightning and Coronal Cloak, and the dragon can comando Lightning once per turn as a single action (instead of a free action that requires using Draconic Frenzy or Lanzando un conjuro).

action->Galvanic Barrage.name: Galvanic Barrage
action->Galvanic Barrage.description: The dragon exhales a massive bolt of lightning at one criatura within 100 pies, dealing @Damage[12d12[electricity]] daño with a @Check[reflex|dc:44|basic] salvación. The lightning then arcs to a criatura of the dragon's choice within 60 pies of the previous target with the same effect. The dragon can't target the same criatura more than once, and they must have line of effect to all targets. The bolt can continue to arc this way until the dragon runs out of targets or until a target critically succeeds at their save. The dragon can't use Galvanic Barrage again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Galvanic Barrage]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Smooth Flying.name: Smooth Flying
action->Smooth Flying.description: The stormcrown dragon doesn't fall if they don't Fly during their turn, and they're unaffected by strong winds or similar effects unless they elige to be.

action->Storm Howl.name: Storm Howl
action->Storm Howl.description: Siempre que a criatura critically fails a save against one of the stormcrown dragon's abilities that deals daño de electricidad, that criatura is also permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened}.

action->Galvanic Barrage.name: Galvanic Barrage

action->Storm Howl.name: Storm Howl

Stormcrown Dragon (Young).name: Stormcrown Dragon (Young)
Stormcrown Dragon (Young).publicNotes:
Heralds of—and heralded by—the primal forces of thunder and lightning, stormcrown dragons meld the majesty of fierce storms and mighty dragons. Driven by emotion and curiosity, these mercurial dragons can change from friend to foe or threatening to thoughtful in mere moments.

While no strangers to the personality rasgos for which dragons are well-known—pride, imperiousness, desire for lovely things, and so on—stormcrown dragons are by NATURE gregarious, even jovial. Indeed, these dragons often mingle with local communities or extend invitations for everything from raucous feasts to elegant soirees. To offend a stormcrown dragon, however, is most unwise. Insults to the dragon's hospitality or friendship, assertions of authority, and demands on them are all likely to elicit a tempestuous response, in every sense of the word. Cursed metamorphosis is a personal favorite of older stormcrown dragons for the disrespectful and demanding, forcing shapes on them more befitting their insignificance. A stormcrown dragon's fury often passes as suddenly as it arises, however, particularly when dulled by a suitable display of contrition.

Taljjae.name: Taljjae
Taljjae.publicNotes: El form de Taljjae's cuerpo puede vary de visit a visit o even moment a moment, but ello's easily recognized due a su signature cloak y masks. So long as Taljjae's mood es placid, ello puede be approached safely, but su mercurial temperament puede be hard a predict.

action->Exit Stage.name: Salir del escenario
action->Exit Stage.description:
Desencadenante Taljjae is reduced to 0 Puntos de Golpe

Efecto Taljjae retains 1 Hit Point and teleports to an empty space within 30 pies. One of its masks remains behind and is broken.

action->Jelly Gluttony.name: Jelly Gluttony
action->Jelly Gluttony.description: If Taljjae detects buckwheat jelly with its jelly sense, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the food and the criatura possessing it (if applicable) and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Desprevenido} to all other criaturas for [[/gmr 1d4 #Rounds]]{1d4 rounds}, or until it uses an appropriate number of INTERACT actions to consume the jelly (generally 2: 1 to take the jelly, and another to eat it). If there's more than one helping of jelly, the condition ends once Taljjae consumes the jelly once.

action->Jelly Sense.name: Jelly Sense
action->Jelly Sense.description: Taljjae has scent as a precise sense out to 120 pies, but only to detect buckwheat jelly, the only food Taljjae loves more than flesh.

action->Change Characters.name: Change Characters
action->Change Characters.description:
Frecuencia una vez por asalto

Efecto Taljjae removes its current mask and dons a new one. The change refreshes Taljjae, restoring 25 Puntos de Golpe. Once Taljjae has removed a mask, it can't Change Characters back to that mask until it has worn all of its unbroken masks at least once, after which the cycle starts again. Taljjae can't don a broken mask.

When Taljjae Changes Characters, it gains access to the listed abilities. Any items (such as armas) associated with its previous mask immediately disappear and are replaced by fresh ones for its new mask, but the effects of any mask abilities it has active persist. Removing a mask and later reapplying it doesn't restore any limited-use abilities.

action->Prop Master.name: Prop Master
action->Prop Master.description: Taljjae has access to the critical specialization effects of any armas it wields from one of its masks.

action->Second Act.name: Second Act
action->Second Act.description:
Desencadenante Taljjae's turn begins Requisitos Taljjae has 200 or fewer Puntos de Golpe

Efecto Taljjae's dance reaches a frantic climax, allowing it to change personas rapidly. Taljjae Changes Characters.

Tehialai-Thief-of-Ships.name: Tehialai-Thief-of-Ships
Tehialai-Thief-of-Ships.publicNotes: Though su current form es but un pequeno y pale shell de su former glory, Tehialai es un legend even en su waning dias. El titanic crustacean wears el hulls de ruined ships as su shell, ripped into shape by vessel-rending garras, as nothing else en Golarion's oceans es grande enough a escudo su cuerpo-o perhaps nothing else va a satisfy su. Few ships puede withstand su might, y fewer still son prepared for su appearance. Those who don't know de el thief de ships won't know a watch for su coming, y those who do know Tehialai offer su tribute a ward off su predation.

strike-ranged->Salt Darts.name: Salt Darts

action->Exoskeletal Armory.name: Exoskeletal Armory
action->Exoskeletal Armory.description: At the beginning of each day, Tehialai can molt to change the morph of her two massive striking claws. She chooses two morphs and adds their Golpes and Release Claw effects to the stat block presented here. Tehialai can molt two different claws or two copies of the same claw.

action->Ship Armor.description: Tehialai hides within a shell made of all the ships she has stolen. Este ship armor reduces any daño Tehialai takes by an amount equal to its Hardness. Once Tehialai is reduced to fewer than half her Puntos de Golpe, or immediately upon being damaged by a impacto crítico, her ship armor breaks, removing her Hardness and reducing her ARMOR CLASS to 32.

action->Capsize.description: Tehialai attempts to capsize an aquatic vessel of her size or smaller that she's adjacent to. She must succeed at a @Check[athletics|dc:33] check (reduced by 5 for each size smaller the vessel is) or the pilot's Sailing LORE DC, whichever is higher.

Efecto Tehialai claims nearby ship pieces to rebuild her home. She destroys the adjacent ship and rebuilds her ship armor, restoring her Hardness and increasing her AC back to 36.

Efecto Tehialai draws water into the base of one of her claws, building immense hydraulic pressure as she prepares to attack. The claw remains loaded until she Releases that Claw or 1 minuto has passed, whichever comes first. While the claw is Pressurized, Tehialai can't use that claw to Golpe. If Tehialai isn't at least partially within a body of water when she Pressurizes her Claw, she takes a -2 penalización to any tiradas de ataque and DCs when she Releases that Claw.

action->Release Claw.description:
Requisitos Tehialai has Pressurized a Claw

Efecto Tehialai lashes out with the force of the sea. See each claw for its released effect; the DC for any effect is 33. After Releasing a Claw, the claw depressurizes.

action->Release Claw (Barbed Spear).name: Release Claw (Barbed Spear)
action->Release Claw (Barbed Spear).description:
Requisitos Tehialai has Pressurized a Claw

All criaturas in a @Template[line|distance:40] take @Damage[8d6[piercing]] daño (@Check[reflex|dc:33|basic] salvación); criaturas that critically fail are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} until the end of Tehialai's next turn.

After Releasing a Claw, the claw depressurizes.

action->Release Claw (Boiling Club).name: Release Claw (Boiling Club)
action->Release Claw (Boiling Club).description:
Requisitos Tehialai has Pressurized a Claw

The impact of Tehialai's claw begets a burning vacuum. Tehialai makes a boiling club Golpe against one target within 15 pies. If she hits, a shock wave booms out, dealing @Damage[3d6[fire]] daño and @Damage[3d6[sonic]] daño to all criaturas except her within @Template[burst|distance:15]{15 pies of el objetivo}, including el objetivo itself (@Check[fortitude|dc:33|basic] salvación). If the Golpe was a impacto crítico, el objetivo uses the degree of success one lower than it rolled on its save. Unlike most fire abilities, this ability can be used underwater, and the typical 5 fire resistance for being underwater doesn't apply.

After Releasing a Claw, the claw depressurizes.

action->Release Claw (Salt Darts).name: Release Claw (Salt Darts)
action->Release Claw (Salt Darts).description: Tehialai launches a flurry of darts. She makes two salt dart Golpes against two different criaturas. Both attacks count towards her multiple attack penalización, but she doesn't increase her penalización until after she has made both attacks.

action->Release Claw (Tidal Gourd).name: Release Claw (Tidal Gourd)
action->Release Claw (Tidal Gourd).description: Tehialai atomizes the water in her claw to create a mist that fills a @Template[emanation|distance:40] centered on her and that lasts until the end of her next turn or until dispersed by a strong wind. All criaturas within the mist become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Oculto}, and all criaturas outside the mist become concealed to criaturas within it. Wavesense functions through the mist and ignores the concealment.

action->Release Claw (Toothed Shredder).name: Release Claw (Toothed Shredder)
action->Release Claw (Toothed Shredder).description: Tehialai's claw whirs and spins to cut through armor and ship hulls. Tehialai makes a toothed shredder Golpe. On a hit, el objetivo queda @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Desprevenido} until the end of Tehialai's next turn and takes @Damage[2d12[bleed]].

Tempest-Sun Mage.name: Tempest-Sun Mage
Tempest-Sun Mage.publicNotes:
A wooden mask carved with a stoic leopard's features covers the face of this scholar. Her long cloak is embroidered with the names of fellow tribe members.

The Tempest-Sun Mages are the chosen protectors of the Magaambya academy and the lands that surround it, watching from the skies for any sign of incursion approaching from the surrounding jungle. They are known as much for the close bonds that they form with their companions as for their extensive knowledge of magical forces, and many mages inscribe the names of important allies on their clothing or gear as reminders of the reason for their vigilance and dedication. The diligence and power of the Tempest-Sun Mages has ensured that no invading force has ever come within 20 miles of the university they defend.

When the Tempest-Sun Mages are not defending the academy itself or accompanying envoys or teachers to distant locales, they use their mastery of arcane and primal magic to keep watch in the surrounding city and beyond, keeping an eye on the balance of power throughout the whole of the Mwangi Expanse. Este magical INTELLIGENCE often allows them to foresee threats to the academy or any nearby towns before such threats can even organize and approach.

While Tempest-Sun Mages generally prefer to disable or incapacitate enemies, and readily call upon on their companions from the Uzunjati to reason with foes when possible, they do not hesitate to unleash lethal force against dangerous or implacable enemies, often taking to the air and raining down elemental fury. In particular, these mages have little tolerance for demons, having previously suffered attacks from the worshippers of the demon lord Angazhan who inhabit the city of Usaro.

Incredible events have rocked the lands of Avistan over the past 10 years, from whole cities reappearing out of a loop in time to magical explosions vaporizing the prison of Gallowspire. Estos marvels, both terrible and awe inspiring, inevitably attracted the attention of the Magaambya academy, home of scholars of magic in all its forms. Scholars, emissaries, and spies alike have now established Magaambyan centers in the north, seeking to learn and to help those they can along the way.

Temteki.name: Temteki
Temteki.publicNotes: Though it superficially resembles a cypress tree and is easily mistaken for an arboreal or other similar plant criatura, Temteki is actually an earth elemental, a criatura of living earth and stone. In normal situations, Temteki is content to remain still and blend into the jungle when observing other criaturas, using its natural camouflage to assist in harrying those it considers interlopers disturbing its home. Temteki usually dissuades such intruders with a combination of surprise attacks and nonlethal snares; the elemental is more interested in getting them to leave than in dealing them any permanent harm. However, to those who prove determined to harm Temteki or its home, Temteki can be an implacable foe. Temteki's asymmetrical gait and appearance often alarm and confuse criaturas who aren't expecting to spot it, especially since it's surprisingly stealthy for its size and appearance.

The Bloodstorm.name: La Tormenta de Sangre
The Bloodstorm.publicNotes:
A hundred thousand leeches, mosquitos, and parasites form a roiling mass of hunger and malice. It moves like a storm through the tunnels and caverns of the Emperor's Peak, constantly in search of its next meal. Though it has many bodies, it has just one, startlingly clever mind. The flames and smoke of the cities keeps it at bay, but in the darkness, it is at home. The dwarves of Highhelm have learned how to live with the threat, but those traveling deeper into the mountain must always remain vigilant.

In the swamps of the Tanglebriar, food is difficult to come by. So when a grievously wounded demon, a shemhazian known as Gratheyr, fled into its waters to escape from his enemies, every starving criatura swarmed at the smell of blood. As the criaturas devoured his flesh, they were corrupted by his Abyssal blood, and their hunger only grew. They feasted until nothing but his heart remained, still beating at the center of the swarm, binding it to a single will. With its meal finished, the bloated swarm left the swamp in search of its next prey. It moved aimlessly, hunting animals and travelers alike, until a great rumble beneath the earth attracted its attention. The Bloodstorm followed the vibrations deep underground, toward the scent of sweat and the sounds of voices.

The Great Flood.name: The Great Flood
The Great Flood.publicNotes:
There are few criaturas capable of such ecological destruction while staying as humorous and lighthearted as the Great Flood. The Great Flood towers with their giant serpent body and nine humanoid heads, each one with a different personality, though all serve the same purpose—to vanquish all signs of life that shouldn't be where they are. Este criatura intends to maintain the balance of the universe, ensuring that nothing takes up more space than necessary. Unfortunately, the judgment of where someone or something should be is only seen and weighed by the 18 eyes of the Great Flood, with little regard to mortal input.

The Great Flood is an immortal, or at least ageless, being who hibernates for 12 years at a stretch. On the thirteenth year, they emerge from the depths of the oceans and begin weighing the state of the world and the environments closest to their resting place: should the first thing they see on dry land be destroyed? Each of the Great Flood's nine heads lends their thoughts and insights to this deliberation, and upon reaching a consensus, they'll either carry on to the next location or they'll drown the land, immersing miles of dry land in salty waters from the ocean. In instances where they perceive the excess life as particularly problematic, they'll even decide to poison the waters with their bitter breath to ensure that nothing survives the judgment they've decreed. The Great Flood, despite its inherently destructive NATURE, isn't actually bloodthirsty and will often afford an opportunity for poor townsfolk to state their case and beg for the lives of their town to be saved. While the Great Flood has the capacity for mercy and consideration, the godlike criatura stands adamant once they've made their decision. One or two of the heads might feel a twinge of guilt and tell a small joke to the townsfolk, relieving themselves of the mental pressure, before murdering an entire village.

The nine personalities of the serpentine criatura often run into contention with each other. One is a perfectionist, while another is aloof; one is assertive, while another is playful; one is capricious, while another is suspicious; one is ambitious, while the other is a people pleaser. The last one is quiet and secretive, only ever whispering to the heads closest to them. Though the heads squabble like siblings, they eventually always make a compromise.
The Great Flood.privateNotes:
Passing Judgment

There are no exact criteria or written rules that drive the Great Flood's decisions. It's a matter of aesthetics, opinion, and which head ends up leading the discussion. Generally, however, settlements at odds with their natural surroundings will be treated more harshly.

A Terrible Sense of Humor

A scholar who debated the Great Flood once recorded the following deadpan exchange, serving more as an example of the criatura's infamous jokes than providing any actual knowledge.

Scholar: "What lord or power do tú answer to?"

The Great Flood: "We don't have a lord."

Scholar: "Then which of tu nine faces is tu leader?"

The Great Flood: "We don't have a leader."

Scholar: "Then how do tú resolve tu disputes?"

The Great Flood: "We don't have disputes."

Tidepool Dragonet.name: Dragoncillo de poza de marea
Tidepool Dragonet.publicNotes:
Tidepool dragonets are lithe, eel-like sovereigns of their miniature tidal territories. Found in the marine environments that their name suggests, tidepool dragonets have strong jaws adapted to cracking open shells. While shellfish are their main food source, they are adaptive foragers. They'll happily catch and eat octopuses, tidal fish, starfish, sea anemones, and seabirds if the opportunity arises. Their long, webbed claws make them nimble hunters and allow them to reach into rocky recesses. They have muscular wings that work well both above and below water.

Tidepool dragonets are proud bullies who habitually harass wildlife and fishers. They frequently steal brightly painted floats, flags, and shiny hooks to decorate their tidal caves. Prized pieces are reserved for ornamenting themselves, and they cover their scales with shards of glass, necklaces of coral, or crowns of silverware retrieved from wrecks.

Though dragonets are smaller and lacking the raw power of great dragons, they are every bit as varied and fascinating as their larger relatives. Like dragons, dragonets have strong ties to magic. Estos ties influence the contrasting natures exhibited by different dragonet types. For example, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.QIXc18xHrEWDmtKW]{Fey Dragonets} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core-2.Actor.Zh8awPHA7DZxTboc]{House Drakes} make fascinating pets and companions, and thus are a popular familiar for spellcasters. Tidepool dragonets, on the other hand, are arrogant and untamable.

Assuming dragonets are harmless due to their size, or the fact that they often live near people, is dangerous. Pest drakes, for instance, are weak and shy individually but are inclined to form dangerous swarms when unsettled. By contrast, pearl dragonets are gentle oddities that seem naturally friendly.

Dragonets range in size from little bigger than songbirds to no larger than house cats. Unlike most great dragons, they stop growing after reaching maturity. They vary greatly in INTELLIGENCE; fey dragonets are known for their tricks and wit, while feral racing drakes have the average problem solving capacity of a pigeon. Each type of dragonet has its own lairing and hoarding habits, and they have unique abilities that reveal their magical NATURE.

Time Archdragon.name: Time Archdragon
Time Archdragon.publicNotes:
Some time dragons would say time is a deep well, with those who explore it dipping cups into the waters at varying depths. Others might say that time is a shattered mirror, each shard reflecting discrete points that can be viewed simultaneously. None would say time is a firm onward march of linear progress, moving inexorably to a predetermined result. Time is fluid and ever-shifting, and time dragons dedicate themselves to protecting its flow.

Although safeguarding the natural temporal order is a mission all time dragons devote themselves to, they go about it in different ways. Staunch traditionalists oppose any meddling with the timestream whatsoever, even to REPAIR daño caused by prior attempts to influence it, viewing this as doing more harm than good. They believe mortals are too short-sighted to responsibly use time magic and might appear without warning to slay those they believe pose a threat to the timestream. Other time dragons attempt to guide the course of events along the path they believe correct while preventing external tampering, often focusing on particular regions, areas of interest, or even individuals

action->Time Portal.description:
Frecuencia once per century

Efecto Over the course of 10 minutos, the time archdragon opens a portal to any point in time and travels through, taking up to 10 criaturas along. The portal remains active for 1 week, connecting the two time periods, though only the time archdragon and criaturas traveling with them can see or pass through it.

action->Chronowarp Aura.name: Chronowarp Aura
action->Chronowarp Aura.description:
30 pies. Time shifts strangely in the presence of a time archdragon. Each criatura starting their turn in the aura must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:43] salvación.

Éxito The criatura is unaffected and temporarily immune for 24 horas.

Fallo The criatura's age advances to elderly or regresses to youth (determined randomly) for 1 asalto. If elderly, the criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2}; if a youth, the criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2}.

Fallo crítico As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 3} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 3}.

action->Decelerating Dodge.description:

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: Cuando el dragón consigue un impacto crítico con un Golpe, recarga Timeshift Breath.

action->Second Chance.name: Segunda Oportunidad
action->Second Chance.description:
Frecuencia una vez por asalto

Desencadenante A criatura within 60 pies (including the time dragon) fails a tirada de salvación or prueba de habilidad

Efecto El objetivo rerolls the check, but must use the second result. El objetivo is then temporarily immune to Second Chance for 24 horas.

action->Temporal Eddies.name: Temporal Eddies
action->Temporal Eddies.description:
Frecuencia once per 10 minutos

Efecto The dragon Strides or Flies up to their Velocidad, leaving behind afterimages of their past and future selves in each space they move through. Until the end of the dragon's next turn, they can use any of these spaces as the origin of their Golpes, conjuros, and other abilities. Observers also perceive the dragon in all these spaces simultaneously and must succeed at a @Check[flat|dc:15] to target the dragon or fail to affect it. A criatura can take a concentrate action to attempt to identify the dragon's true location with a successful @Check[will|dc:46] salvación.

action->Timeshift Breath.name: Timeshift Breath
action->Timeshift Breath.description:
The dragon breathes a blast of temporal energy, warping time in a @Template[type:cone|distance:80]. Las criaturas in the area must attempt a @Check[will|dc:46] salvación. The dragon can't use Timeshift Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Timeshift Breath]]{1d4 rounds}. Éxito crítico The criatura is unaffected.

Éxito The criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 asalto.

Fallo The criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} for 1 asalto.

Fallo crítico The criatura shifts briefly forward in time, vanishing and reappearing at the beginning of the time dragon's next turn in the same location (or an adjacent space if their former location is occupied), unaware that any time has passed. While timeshifted, time pauses for that criatura, and it cannot take actions or be affected by anything else.

action->Bound Limbs.name: Bound Limbs
action->Bound Limbs.description: A torn quartet ordinarily has four severed limbs tethered to a central point by near-incorporeal ropes. A limb is essentially cut away from the central point and rendered nonfunctional each time the torn quartet loses 60 Puntos de Golpe (so at 180 Puntos de Golpe, the torn quartet has three functional limbs, at 120 Puntos de Golpe, it has two functional limbs, and so on). Each functioning limb can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.PMbdMWc2QroouFGD]{Grapple} separate criaturas within reach, or multiple functioning limbs can Grapple the same criatura; for each additional limb used to Grapple a criatura, the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} DC increases by 2.

action->Replacement Parts.name: Replacement Parts
action->Replacement Parts.description: A torn quartet can spend 1 minuto tearing apart the corpse of a humanoid criatura that was killed within the last hour to regain 60 Puntos de Golpe and restore one of its nonfunctioning limbs. A torn quartet can't have more than four limbs.

action->Flurry of Limbs.name: Flurry of Limbs
action->Flurry of Limbs.description: The torn quartet makes a number of limb Golpes up to its number of functioning limbs, each against a different target. Estos attacks count toward the torn quartet's multiple attack penalización, but the multiple attack penalización doesn't increase until after the torn quartet makes all its attacks.

action->Split Reactions.name: Split Reactions
action->Split Reactions.description: A torn quartet has a number of reactions per round equal to its number of still-functioning limbs, which it can use only to make Reactive Golpes. It can't use more than 1 reaction on the same triggering action, even if a criatura leaves several squares within its reach, and the torn quartet must use a different limb for each Reactive Golpe it makes. Siempre que one of the torn quartet's limbs is rendered nonfunctional, the torn quartet loses one of its reactions.

action->Tear Asunder.name: Tear Asunder
action->Tear Asunder.description:
Requisitos The torn quartet has a criatura grappled or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by at least two limbs

Efecto The criatura takes @Damage[5d6[slashing]] daño for each limb currently grabbing or restraining it (maximum 15d6), with a @Check[fortitude|dc:30|basic] salvación. On a critical failure, the criatura also loses a random body part, and one of the torn quartet's limbs is now no longer grabbing or restraining it.

Twilight Talon Infiltrator Team.name: Twilight Talon Infiltrator Team
Twilight Talon Infiltrator Team.publicNotes: Estos teams of elite Andoren field agents possess specialized training in executing covert operations. Many have recently been dispatched to Isger to assist the insurgents of the Hellbreakers League in throwing off the yoke of Chelaxian oppression.

action->Now!!.name: Now!!
action->Now!!.description:
Desencadenante A criatura moves adjacent to the infiltrators or takes a hostile action against them

Requisitos The infiltrators are disguised

Efecto The infiltrators cast aside their disguises and unleash a 2-action Blindside against all enemies in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5]. A criatura that critically fails the save takes an additional 1d6 daño de precisión.

action->Undercover.name: Undercover
action->Undercover.description: By spending 2 hours preparing disguises, performing reconnaissance, and the like, the infiltrators can convincingly impersonate any troop unit of their level or lower that has the humanoid rasgo. Alternatively, they can disguise themselves as a mixed assortment of humanoid noncombatants who don't obviously form a cohesive unit. Este functions as the Impersonate action with the infiltrators gaining a +2 bonificador de circunstancia to their DECEPTION DC. Infiltrators can't use Undercover to appear as specific individuals, nor can they impersonate groups that require resources unavailable to them, at the GM's discretion (impersonating a cavalry unit without access to mounts, for example).

action->Blindside.name: Blindside
action->Blindside.description:
1 to 3

Frecuencia una vez por asalto

Efecto The infiltrators strike against enemies in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5], dealing daño of a type appropriate to any armas or implements incorporated into their disguise, with a @Check[reflex|dc:23|basic] salvación. The daño depends on the number of actions.

1 @Damage[(1d8+1)[bludgeoning]]{1d8+1 bludgeoning, piercing, or daño cortante}

2 @Damage[(2d8+8)[bludgeoning]]{2d8+8 bludgeoning, piercing, or daño cortante}

3 @Damage[(3d8+9)[bludgeoning]]{3d8+9 bludgeoning, piercing, or daño cortante}

action->Faces in the Crowd.name: Faces in the Crowd
action->Faces in the Crowd.description: Twilight Talon infiltrators are masters of blending into and dispersing seamlessly among large groups. While disguised as noncombatants, they can move into other criaturas' spaces, and other criaturas can move into the team's spaces.

action->Snap Shot.name: Disparo instantáneo
action->Snap Shot.description: The infiltrators draw or reload concealed hand crossbows and launch a hail of bolts in a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] within 60 pies that deals @Damage[5d6[piercing]|options:area-damage] daño (@Check[reflex|dc:23|basic] salvación). When the unit is reduced to 2 segments, this area decreases to a @Template[type:burst|distance:5].

Ugvashi.name: Ugvashi
Ugvashi.publicNotes:
Estos razor-plated pangolins—about the size of small ponies—are the traditional pack animals of halflings from Casmaron, though the ugvashi's serrated plates and tendency to curl up make them ill-suited as mounts. Ugvashi first arrived in the Impossible Lands onboard the Thousand and One ships of Maharajah Khiben-Sald, alongside peafowl, giant squirrels, and other fauna from Vudra. In the modern day, ugvashi are such a recognized sight that many people forget they aren't a native species. Though some feral populations exist, mainly on the island of Jalmeray, the hostile environs of Nex and the Mana Wastes mean ugvashi mainly appear in domestic settings, usually as working beasts among the Nearic halflings of western Nex.

Though ugvashi are mostly harmless, they're somewhat more dangerous than their smaller cousins, causing a stir when reckless citizens attempt to pet the criaturas. Ugvashi scales are razor sharp, and their large and blunted digging claws can be deadly due to their size. People who attempt to steal the animals or ride them without training often receive moderate cuts for their trouble. However, ugvashi are generally curious and very friendly, and more than one visitor or wilderness explorer has found a baby ugvashi toddling after them and pawing at their boots.

Nearic halflings also paint their ugvashi with distinctive warding patterns and sigils, some of which are actually effective and provide a surprise for opportunistic thieves or predators. Though due consideration is spent on protecting an ugvashi's cargo, the animals themselves have proven to be tempting targets as well, especially for their meat. With blighted landscapes making animal husbandry impractical and magical pollution leaving local seafood with a distinct aftertaste, a number of Nexian and Mana Wastes peoples have developed a taste for ugvashi. Since the animals lack an aggressive temperament, it often falls to their caretakers to discourage such predations through whatever means necessary.

Ugvashi shed their scales each winter, allowing for the plates to be collected safely and turned into quality armor and other pieces of craftwork. Nearic halflings rarely trade or sell these items, however, out of fear that they might lead to more people trying to steal their ugvashi.

action->Defensive Curl.name: Defensive Curl
action->Defensive Curl.description: The ugvashi coils into a ball to defend itself. It gains a +2 bonificador de circunstancia to AC. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.FjcvJWPFwkyy5vEk]{Efecto: Artificer's comando}

action->Artificer's Eye.name: Artificer's Eye
action->Artificer's Eye.description: Ulistul chooses one construct or statue she can currently perceive with a precise sense or with statuesense; usually, her only precise sense is vision. After choosing her target, she begins to perceive el objetivo's surroundings as though she occupied its space. If el objetivo is either an inanimate statue or a mindless criatura, she can also verbally INTERACT with nearby criaturas (including issuing Artificer's Commands) or cause el objetivo to move subtly, such as moving its mouth. Este ability can be sustained indefinitely as long as Ulistul can perceive el objetivo, though her visual stimuli from her own body are harder to process; she's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} when using her own senses for the effect's duration.

action->Dismantler.name: Dismantler
action->Dismantler.description: Ulistul's attacks against constructs and objects gain the deadly d12 rasgo and ignore up to 10 of el objetivo's Hardness and resistances.

action->Ivory Dictum.name: Ivory Dictum
action->Ivory Dictum.description: Ulistul takes control of a construct within 30 pies. Este has the effects of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OsOhx3TGIZ7AhD0P]{Dominate}(@Check[will|dc:32]) but can affect mindless criaturas and ignores el objetivo's golem antimagic, if any.

Umbral Archdragon.name: Umbral Archdragon
Umbral Archdragon.publicNotes:
Stories across Golarion warn children about the monsters that dwell in the shadows, but no story captures the reality of the umbral dragon. Natives of the Netherworld, these occult dragons are at home in the darkness, using it to their advantage both in and out of battle. Umbral dragons rarely worry about fighting fairly, emerging from hiding to strike unwary foes and using their magical breath without compunction. Similarly, in social situations, they often remain in the shadows, operating through other criaturas. Even in direct conversation, they frequently obscure their true intent, preferring to avoid ever being pinned down with a solid answer.

While umbral dragons are rarely altruistic, their preferred diet creates a strange dichotomy that attracts other criaturas to them as a potential source of safety, especially in the Netherworld. While much of the multiverse sees undead as a dire threat, for umbral dragons, undead are a tasty snack. Umbral dragons find the flavor of necrotic flesh irresistible and the void energy of incorporeal undead a potent spice, making them one of the few criaturas in existence known to hunt the unliving as a source of food.
Umbral Archdragon.saveDetails: +2 a todas las salvaciones contra sombra

Oscuridad (a voluntad)

action->Hide in Shadows.name: Hide in Shadows
action->Hide in Shadows.description: El dragón puede Esconderse con luz tenue incluso si no tiene cobertura.

action->Voidsense.name: Voidsense
action->Voidsense.description: The dragon can taste animating void energy, allowing them to sense criaturas with curación de vacío as a precise sense. It can also sense incorporeal criaturas with curación de vacío, like shadows, when they are inside solid objects.

action->Pin Shadow.name: Pin Shadow
action->Pin Shadow.description:
Desencadenante A criatura within reach of the dragon's claw uses a move action or leaves a square during a move action it's using

Requisitos The triggering criatura is in bright light or dim light and has a shadow

Efecto The dragon makes a claw Golpe against the triggering criatura. On a hit, the trigger criatura also has its shadow pinned in place, restricting its movement. The criatura treats the area of the dragon's aura as difficult terrain until it uses an INTERACT action to unpin its shadow. If the area was already difficult terrain, the criatura treats it as greater difficult terrain.

action->Tenacious Shadows.name: Tenacious Shadows
action->Tenacious Shadows.description: Shadows fill attacker's eyes. Any criatura that must attempt a prueba plana to target the dragon because of dim light must roll twice and use the worse result.

action->Umbral Pall.name: Umbral Pall
action->Umbral Pall.description: 120 pies. Shadows surround the dragon. The radius of all light from light sources and the areas of light conjuros in the aura are halved. The shadows also cling to criaturas, making areas of dim light difficult terrain.

action->Devour Undead.name: Devour Undead
action->Devour Undead.description: The dragon's jaws Golpes have the benefit of a ghost touch property rune and deal an additional 8d6 daño de fuerza to undead.

action->Draconic Frenzy.name: Frenesí Dracónico
action->Draconic Frenzy.description: El dragón realiza dos Golpes de garra y un Golpe de cola en cualquier orden.

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: El dragón recarga Tenebrous Breath siempre que consigue un impacto crítico con un Golpe.

action->Drain Vigor.name: Drain Vigor
action->Drain Vigor.description:
When the dragon deals daño de vacío to a living criatura with its jaws Golpe, the umbral dragon gains 20 temporary HP that last for 1 minuto and the criatura must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:44] salvación or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} on a critical failure). Further daño dealt by the dragon's jaws Golpe increases the drained condition value by 1 on a failed save (2 on a critical failure), to a maximum of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 4}.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.wBFtXxByOza6N9hs]{Efecto: Drain Vigor}

action->Tenebrous Breath.name: Tenebrous Breath
action->Tenebrous Breath.description:
The umbral dragon exhales in one of two ways. They can't use Tenebrous Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Tenebrous Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.

  • Darkness (occult, void) The dragon breathes a blast of darkness that deals @Damage[24d6[void]|options:area-damage] daño in a @Template[type:cone|distance:60] (@Check[reflex|dc:46|basic|traits:occult,void] salvación). Undead criaturas take @Damage[24d6[force]|options:area-damage]{force} daño instead of daño de vacío.

  • Shadows (occult, shadow) The dragon breathes a blast of shadows in a @Template[type:cone|distance:60]. Each criatura within the cone must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:46|traits:occult,shadow] salvación.

    Éxito crítico The criatura is unaffected.

    Éxito The criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 4} for 1 asalto.

    Fallo The criatura is debilitado 4 for 1 minuto.

Underworld Archdragon.name: Underworld Archdragon
Underworld Archdragon.publicNotes:
If there are any imperial dragons who benefited from moving out of their native elemental plane, it's underworld dragons. Once related solely to the element of fire, early underworld dragons harnessed elemental forces through arcane means for reasons no longer remembered. With each subsequent generation, both their arcane power and mastery over the elements grew. Their efforts were later bolstered by their studies in alchemy, which allowed dragons to cultivate themselves even further with various mutagens and elixirs.

Today, though their NATURE is primarily still connected with the element of fire, an underworld dragon can consume wood with ease, threaten entire regions with quakes, lay claim to the minerals and gems in the rocks and stone, and die to form volcanoes that create more land masses. Some even flippantly snort at the lapping waves of the sea, not fearing any retaliation from the sea dragon nations nor their kings. Though their powers might be relatively weaker than another imperial dragon of the same age, their mastery of many elements and the arcane arts makes underworld dragons formidable opponents.

Until the end of their next turn, they take a –1 penalización de circunstancia to tiradas de ataque, and their jaws Golpes don't deal daño de fuego. Este limitation ends if the dragon uses Exploding Red Breath.

If the underworld dragon takes daño from a conjuro with the cold or water rasgo, the elemental magic of fire within them is momentarily dampened. Until the end of their next turn, they take a –1 penalización de circunstancia to tiradas de ataque, and their jaws Golpes don't deal daño de fuego. Este limitation ends if the dragon uses Exploding Red Breath.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.81XYZZ3H0GL8thdQ]{Efecto: Countered by Water}

action->Fed by Wood.name: Fed by Wood
action->Fed by Wood.description:
When an underworld dragon is struck by a arma made primarily of wood or affected by a conjuro with the plant or wood rasgo, the dragon’s internal fiery essences are stoked with the added fuel. Their Exploding Red Breath recharges, and the daño de fuego from the dragon’s jaws deals an additional die of daño until the end of the dragon’s next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.4FMFRlEC923CnLI7]{Efecto: Fed by Wood}
