Veteran Reclaimer.name: Veteran Reclaimer
Veteran Reclaimer.publicNotes:
Este grizzled half-orc wields a longbow with the familiarity of a woman who considers it more as an extension of her body than a arma.

When Lastwall fell, many of the former Knights of Ozem became disheartened and scattered, wandering aimlessly through the wilds of the Inner Sea. Though the horrific events that led to the fall of Lastwall shook their faith in the traditional hierarchy of the Knights, they hardened their resolve to hunt all undead from the face of Golarion. Estos Crimson Reclaimers still see the Whispering Tyrant as their primary foe, but they can be found in many of the most haunted regions of the world, living off the land and hunting the restless dead.

While heroism and fervor for their cause still burns in their heart, veteran reclaimers have lived long enough to lose their taste for tales of courtly valor and valiant last stands. They have learned the value of caution and thus engage their enemies from range and use terrain to their advantage. They are quick to strike back at enemies that harm their allies, knowing staunch teammates are essential in the face of the world's many horrors.

Though the nation of Lastwall is shattered and its leaders have fled, the courage of those who once defended its shining walls remains strong. The Knights of Lastwall are found in places of great calamity, escorting civilians and beating back the undead. Should the PCs ever venture into a crisis zone, they may likely as not see the Knights of Lastwall there as well, be they forming an armored wall to defend the innocent or creeping through deathly wastelands where even the bravest know mortal fear. Unless the PCs are evil or unwitting dupes of Tar-Baphon's agents, the Whispering Way, these knights mostly serve as precious allies in realms where friendly faces are rare. The virtuous defender could be a member of a knightly squad or a recruiter seeking those willing to risk their lives to save Avistan from a terrible peril. The veteran reclaimer is likely found in the depths of the Gravelands or other truly forsaken realms, where even the slightest misstep can lead to death or worse. Such cunning but virtuous souls might request help leading people to safety, act as a guide through unknown territory, or offer valuable advice and information about dangerous criaturas or traps the PCs might risk encountering.
Veteran Reclaimer.speed: ignores the effects of non-magical difficult terrain

Virtuous Defender.name: Virtuous Defender
Virtuous Defender.publicNotes:
With his well-worn plate armor and mighty shield, this tall figure appears ready to stand against any foe.

Even with the fall of the nation of Lastwall, many people still dedicate their lives to opposing the forces and schemes of the Whispering Tyrant. Styling themselves the Shining Sentinels, they see themselves as a bulwark against the further spread of the Tyrant's influence. When not rallying troops to battle against their sworn foe or protecting villages from undead incursions, these knights travel the Inner Sea in hopes of recruiting other righteous souls to fight against the undead hordes.

Many Shining Sentinels are servants of good deities, such as Iomedae; in battle, they turn their god-given powers against their foes. Estos virtuous warriors put the safety of their companions before their own and often hold defensive positions to protect their allies.

Though the nation of Lastwall is shattered and its leaders have fled, the courage of those who once defended its shining walls remains strong. Vizier Archdragon.name: Vizier Archdragon
Vizier Archdragon.publicNotes:
There's a feeling every teacher knows. It's when one has taken a young mind and educated, entrenado, and molded them to one's specifications before setting them loose and watching the pupil act on one's teachings. It's a feeling of creation, control, and wonder, the knowledge that one has created this great and glorious thing—and if one has done the job exceptionally well, then the student will outshine the maestro. Este is immortality and power, and this is what vizier dragons chase.

Vizier dragons are primarily concerned with the education and cultivation of people. People fascinate vizier dragons in all their riotous, contradictory complexity. Why do some people excel, and others falter and fail? Why does one person become a saint and the next a tyrant? Why do some become legends in their own time, while others labor in ignominy?
Vizier Archdragon.saveDetails: +1 de estado a todas las salvaciones contra magia

Vorpal Archdragon.name: Vorpal Archdragon
Vorpal Archdragon.publicNotes:
Vorpal dragons were not created by some ancient divinity nor born of a specific realm or force. Their birth was an arcane accident, the result of unstoppable magic contacting immovable beast. In unknowable ancient ages, the first jabberwock was wrought by the Eldest and the first vorpal sword was wrought in turn to slay the beast. When that very first blade went snicker-snack for the very first time, tasting the primeval lifeblood of the draconic Tane, the first vorpal dragon was born.

Vorpal dragons are most notorious for their keen vorpal magic. Even the least of these dragons can sever a foe's head in a single lucky stroke. Unusually, however, the subject survives as a bipartite criatura: a headless body controlled by a detached head that still thinks and speaks, and which can outlive said body's destruction. It's not uncommon for would-be dragonslayers to be sent home carrying their own heads under one arm as a lesson in humility. The unluckier ones, alas, may be kept as trophies—and, in a very literal sense, conversation pieces—while the dragon devours their greater portion. Some might even wear their favorite severed heads as a macabre necklace.

action->Draconic Frenzy.name: Frenesí Dracónico
action->Draconic Frenzy.description: El dragón realiza dos Golpes de garra y un Golpe de cola en cualquier orden.

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: El dragón recarga Feast of Blood siempre que consigue un impacto crítico con un Golpe.

action->Dragon's Teeth.name: Dragon's Teeth
action->Dragon's Teeth.description:
Frecuencia una vez al día

Efecto A vorpal archdragon never fights alone save by choice, for within their pinioned wings an army of armaments stands ever ready. With a snap of their wings, the archdragon rains blades across the battlefield in a @Template[type:line|distance:100], dealing @Damage[22d6[slashing]|options:area-damage] daño with a @Check[reflex|dc:44|basic] salvación. Estos blades are partially animated and remain in the area for 10 minutos, during which time the area is considered greater difficult terrain for every criatura except for the archdragon. Any criatura that enters the area or begins their turn within or adjacent to this area takes @Damage[(4d8+16)[slashing]|options:area-damage] daño (@Check[reflex|dc:44|basic] salvación).

action->Feast of Blood.name: Feast of Blood
action->Feast of Blood.description: The dragon inhales sharply, pulling blood from wounds and into the dragon's maw. Each criatura in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] takes their current daño persistente de sangrado plus @Damage[14d6[void]|options:area-damage] daño (@Check[will|dc:45|basic] salvación). The dragon gains Puntos de Golpe temporales equal to half the greatest amount of daño de vacío dealt to a single criatura this way. The dragon can't use Feast of Blood again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Feast of Blood]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Gruesome Cuts.name: Gruesome Cuts
action->Gruesome Cuts.description: Persistent daño de sangrado inflicted by the dragon, even magically, carries a poison that inhibits clotting. Healing the criatura to full HP doesn't end the bleeding, the DC of any prueba plana to recover is 2 higher, and the DC to stop the bleeding using Administer First Aid is 40. Este poison can be counteracted (DC 41), and successfully doing so ends the bleeding.

action->Heads Will Roll!.name: ¡Rodarán cabezas!
action->Heads Will Roll!.description:
Frecuencia una vez por minuto

Efecto The vorpal dragon swoops across the battlefield, sweeping their axe-bladed tail through their foes. The dragon Flies twice; at any point during this movement, the dragon makes up to two chin blade Golpes, each against a different criatura within reach. The dragon's multiple attack penalización doesn't increase until all Golpes are made.

action->Vorpal Binding.name: Vorpal Binding
action->Vorpal Binding.description:
The vorpal dragon beheads its foes—sometimes without killing them. A vorpal dragon's chin blade Golpes count as having the vorpal arma property rune for the purpose of weaknesses. Siempre que the vorpal dragon critically succeeds on a chin blade Golpe, it deals an additional @Damage[6d6[persistent,bleed]] daño, which can be ended normally.

When a vorpal dragon rolls a natural 20 on a chin blade Golpe, el objetivo must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] salvación; this has the incapacitation rasgo. On a failure, the criatura is beheaded. A criatura beheaded this way does not automatically die; instead, their head and body live on, disconnected but mystically linked, with the head controlling the body from afar. A beheaded criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} as they attempt to coordinate movements from an unusual perspective, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 4} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} if their head can't perceive their body from its location. Estos conditions are suppressed if the body holds its head, and don't apply to actions performed exclusively by the head, mind, or voice. If the body is killed, the head can live on, but destroying the head kills the body as well. Este effect can be ended only by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2Vkd1IxylPceUAAF]{Regenerate}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Hnc7eGi7vyZenAIm]{Breath of Life}, or any effect that restores life to the dead; only effects that restore an incomplete corpse will replace an absent or destroyed body, however. The dragon can elige to instantly kill a criatura when beheading them, as per the vorpal arma property rune's activation.

Efecto A vorpal archdragon never fights alone save by choice, for within their pinioned wings an army of armaments stands ever ready. With a snap of their wings, the archdragon rains blades across the battlefield in a @Template[type:line|distance:100], dealing @Damage[22d6[slashing]|options:area-damage] daño with a @Check[reflex|dc:44|basic] salvación. Estos blades are partially animated and remain in the area for 10 minutos, during which time the area is considered greater difficult terrain for every criatura except for the archdragon. Any criatura that enters the area or begins their turn within or adjacent to this area takes @Damage[(4d8+16)[slashing]|options:area-damage] daño (@Check[reflex|dc:44|basic] salvación).

action->Feast of Blood.name: Feast of Blood
action->Feast of Blood.description: The dragon inhales sharply, pulling blood from wounds and into the dragon's maw. Each criatura in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] takes their current daño persistente de sangrado plus @Damage[14d6[void]|options:area-damage] daño (@Check[will|dc:45|basic] salvación). The dragon gains Puntos de Golpe temporales equal to half the greatest amount of daño de vacío dealt to a single criatura this way. The dragon can't use Feast of Blood again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Feast of Blood]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Gruesome Cuts.name: Gruesome Cuts
action->Gruesome Cuts.description: Persistent daño de sangrado inflicted by the dragon, even magically, carries a poison that inhibits clotting. Healing the criatura to full HP doesn't end the bleeding, the DC of any prueba plana to recover is 2 higher, and the DC to stop the bleeding using Administer First Aid is 40. Este poison can be counteracted (DC 41), and successfully doing so ends the bleeding.

action->Heads Will Roll!.name: ¡Rodarán cabezas!
action->Heads Will Roll!.description:
Frecuencia una vez por minuto

Efecto The vorpal dragon swoops across the battlefield, sweeping their axe-bladed tail through their foes. The dragon Flies twice; at any point during this movement, the dragon makes up to two chin blade Golpes, each against a different criatura within reach. The dragon's multiple attack penalización doesn't increase until all Golpes are made.

action->Vorpal Binding.name: Vorpal Binding
action->Vorpal Binding.description:
The vorpal dragon beheads its foes—sometimes without killing them. A vorpal dragon's chin blade Golpes count as having the vorpal arma property rune for the purpose of weaknesses. Siempre que the vorpal dragon critically succeeds on a chin blade Golpe, it deals an additional @Damage[6d6[persistent,bleed]] daño, which can be ended normally.

When a vorpal dragon rolls a natural 20 on a chin blade Golpe, el objetivo must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] salvación; this has the incapacitation rasgo. On a failure, the criatura is beheaded. A criatura beheaded this way does not automatically die; instead, their head and body live on, disconnected but mystically linked, with the head controlling the body from afar. A beheaded criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} as they attempt to coordinate movements from an unusual perspective, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 4} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} if their head can't perceive their body from its location. Estos conditions are suppressed if the body holds its head, and don't apply to actions performed exclusively by the head, mind, or voice. If the body is killed, the head can live on, but destroying the head kills the body as well. Este effect can be ended only by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2Vkd1IxylPceUAAF]{Regenerate}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Hnc7eGi7vyZenAIm]{Breath of Life}, or any effect that restores life to the dead; only effects that restore an incomplete corpse will replace an absent or destroyed body, however. The dragon can elige to instantly kill a criatura when beheading them, as per the vorpal arma property rune's activation.

Vorpal Dragon (Adult).name: Vorpal Dragon (Adult)
Vorpal Dragon (Adult).publicNotes:
Vorpal dragons were not created by some ancient divinity nor born of a specific realm or force. Their birth was an arcane accident, the result of unstoppable magic contacting immovable beast. In unknowable ancient ages, the first jabberwock was wrought by the Eldest and the first vorpal sword was wrought in turn to slay the beast. When that very first blade went snicker-snack for the very first time, tasting the primeval lifeblood of the draconic Tane, the first vorpal dragon was born.

Vorpal dragons are most notorious for their keen vorpal magic. Even the least of these dragons can sever a foe's head in a single lucky stroke. Unusually, however, the subject survives as a bipartite criatura: a headless body controlled by a detached head that still thinks and speaks, and which can outlive said body's destruction. It's not uncommon for would-be dragonslayers to be sent home carrying their own heads under one arm as a lesson in humility. The unluckier ones, alas, may be kept as trophies—and, in a very literal sense, conversation pieces—while the dragon devours their greater portion. Some might even wear their favorite severed heads as a macabre necklace.

Vorpal Dragon (Young, Spellcaster).name: Vorpal Dragon (Young, Spellcaster)
Vorpal Dragon (Young, Spellcaster).publicNotes:
Vorpal dragons were not created by some ancient divinity nor born of a specific realm or force. Their birth was an arcane accident, the result of unstoppable magic contacting immovable beast. In unknowable ancient ages, the first jabberwock was wrought by the Eldest and the first vorpal sword was wrought in turn to slay the beast. When that very first blade went snicker-snack for the very first time, tasting the primeval lifeblood of the draconic Tane, the first vorpal dragon was born.

Vorpal dragons are most notorious for their keen vorpal magic. Even the least of these dragons can sever a foe's head in a single lucky stroke. Unusually, however, the subject survives as a bipartite criatura: a headless body controlled by a detached head that still thinks and speaks, and which can outlive said body's destruction. It's not uncommon for would-be dragonslayers to be sent home carrying their own heads under one arm as a lesson in humility. The unluckier ones, alas, may be kept as trophies—and, in a very literal sense, conversation pieces—while the dragon devours their greater portion. Some might even wear their favorite severed heads as a macabre necklace.

Vorvorak.name: Vorvorak
Vorvorak.publicNotes:
Those trespassing on abandoned canals might come face-to-face with a vorvorak, a large criatura that resembles a dragon or crocodile. Estos territorial beasts keep hoards that they disguise with magical illusions, using their natural talent for spellcasting. Often mistaken for dragons, vorvoraks are commonly referred to as canal dragons or mud dragons. However, they aren't truly related to dragons but rather evolved from local crocodiles and exposure to innate magic in the region of Taldor.

Vorvoraks are solitary criaturas, preferring to hunt in the early morning or early evening. In general, vorvoraks make their lairs in areas with some submersion. Such places let them hide their hordes and use their brown, mossy bodies as a natural form of STEALTH. Due to their evolution and magical contamination, vorvoraks have limited innate magical abilities, allowing them to control the water around them and infuse it with their own poisonous bile.

All vorvoraks share a common rasgo: hoarding treasure. Many fill their lairs with coins, gems, and anything shiny they take from their victims, with some older hoards containing relics of the surrounding imperial nations. The condition of the items is of no importance to the vorvoraks; a hoard is just as likely to contain junk as items of true value.

A fully grown vorvorak is around 24 pies long and weighs approximately 3,000 pounds, with muddy brown scales, a serpentine neck, and hard fins on their back that resemble wings.

Vulture Rat.name: Rata buitre
Vulture Rat.publicNotes:
Estos scavenger rats live in Geb, where they feast on the remains of the undead. They're adapted to going long periods without sustenance but viciously attack any possible food source.

giant rats are enormous versions of the common vermin. They are typically found in abundant numbers, but since they cannot fit in the nooks where mundane rats typically hide, they are much easier to locate and exterminate. They mostly live in sewers where they can scavenge from the streets above, but some families of giant rats live in more remote locations, such as dank caves or forests and hills. Rats are incredibly adept survivors and can be found nearly anywhere in the world, though they tend to favor temperate or warm climates as opposed to cold regions.

Although its bite alone is not lethal except to the very young or very old, the giant rat carries the filth fever common to rodents around the world-a pestilence more than capable of ravaging rural communities.

Wailing Archdragon.name: Wailing Archdragon
Wailing Archdragon.publicNotes:
Canny, patient, and creative, wailing dragons are adepts of sound and psychology. With both their physiology and innate connection to arcane magic allowing them to produce and shape sound waves, these reclusive criaturas are heard much more often than seen. Named for their tendency to use uncanny keening vocalizations to communicate across long distances and startle prey, wailing dragons haunt locations that create interesting or useful echoes, such as canyons or caverns. Though ruthless predators when needed, most wailing dragons devote their energy toward investigating the effects sound has on the environment and the bodies and minds of criaturas.

Minstrels, divas, and tunesmiths seek out these criaturas during their mating season, when two dragons sing courtship ballads full of intricate harmonies. While this might be the PERFORMANCE of a lifetime, it's a dangerous concert, as incautious audience members frequently become meals for the nuptial couple. (The famous Chelaxian composer, Gretezi Valtros, disappeared on such an expedition in 4275 ar, after he set out to teach a wailing dragon High Azlanti and "instruct it in the decorous art of opera.") Most criaturas also find the close-range subsonic vibrations emitted by wailing dragons extremely uncomfortable, reinforcing the idea that it's best to observe them from a distance.

Walcofinde.name: Walcofinde
Walcofinde.publicNotes:
Forever entombed, walcofindes are vengeful undead criaturas inhabiting the enclosed spaces in which they were sealed and eventually perished. As they ultimately succumbed to a slow death by starvation and suffocation, walcofindes are similar to zombies in their hunger and rage. What sets them apart are their vicious claws of stone-sharpened bone, protruding through worn down, fleshless fingers as a result of desperate and futile attempts to escape.

Walcofindes are bound to their death site. Estos "wall-coffined" undead can manifest their forms within the structure where they were sealed, possessing the walls and stealthily traversing along them. Walcofindes' manifestations adopt the patterned appearance of the structure's materials, but not its physical properties. They take the form of hungry, grasping humanoid torsos emerging from the walls like harrowing extensions of their eternal prison. Unable to ever fully leave their structures, these undead are destined to be a part of it forever.

Despite their decaying forms, walcofindes retain the INTELLIGENCE they would've had in life; for example, a walcofinde who was previously a soldier could understand enemigo tactics and assess the appearance and equipment of their foes, allowing them to strategize and prioritize targets as well as organize with other nearby walcofindes to formulate an attack.

action->Sneak Attack.name: Ataque furtivo
action->Sneak Attack.description: A walcofinde deals an additional 1d6 daño de precisión to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Desprevenido} criaturas.

action->Structural Possession.name: Structural Possession
action->Structural Possession.description: A walcofinde can merge themself with any wall they can touch within their sealed chamber and can create a manifestation of themself through any part of that wall on either side within 100 pies. Este manifestation appears as the rotting upper half of the walcofinde protruding from the wall, but their skin is patterned as if they were the same structural material as the wall they're emerging from. While manifested, the walcofinde's claw attack gains a reach of 10 pies, but they can move only by using Wall Glide. Any daño done to the manifestation affects the walcofinde themself. A walcofinde can Dismiss their structural possession to retreat back into their sealed chamber.

action->Wall Blend.name: Wall Blend
action->Wall Blend.description:
Requisitos The walcofinde is manifested using Structural Possession and isn't observed by any enemies

Efecto Until the next time they act, the walcofinde's manifestation changes their visual appearance to match the surrounding wall. They have an automatic result of 31 on their STEALTH checks to Hide.

action->Wall Glide.name: Wall Glide
action->Wall Glide.description:
Requisitos The walcofinde is manifested using Structural Possession

Efecto The walcofinde's manifestation Strides, submerging into the wall and reemerging from the wall at the end of their movement. If the walcofinde takes 2 actions to Wall Glide, their manifestation can Zancada twice before reemerging. In either case, they can move only within walls that are within 100 pies of their sealed chamber.

Whalesteed.name: Ballencel
Whalesteed.publicNotes: Whalesteeds were first tamed in the Shackles as part of an ambush between rival pirate captains. Whalesteed riders are still an unusual sight, as learning to maestro the skill takes years of training.

action->Aquatic Echolocation.name: Aquatic Echolocation
action->Aquatic Echolocation.description: Un whalesteed puede usar su oido as un preciso sentido at el listed alcance, but solo underwater.

action->Deep Breath.name: Contener La Respiración
action->Deep Breath.description: Un whalesteed puede contener la respiracion for 2 horas.

action->Ramming Velocidad.name: Ramming Velocidad
action->Ramming Velocidad.description: The whalesteed @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.c8TGiZ48ygoSPofx]{Swims} twice and then makes a snout Golpe. As long as it moved at least 20 pies, it gains a +1 bonificador de circunstancia to its tirada de ataque. A Large or smaller criatura hit by this attack must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:16] salvación or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 asalto.

Whisper Archdragon.name: Whisper Archdragon
Whisper Archdragon.publicNotes: Whisper dragones son keen collectors de rumors y secrets who spend centuries honing su information networks y relationships. They generally do so no out de un intent a hold el information over others o a usar for su own machinations, but simply because el process de learning y gathering information es fulfilling. Their hoards son sparse compared a those de otro dragones, as ellos hold su true treasures—secrets—en su minds.

spell->Hidden Mind (Constant).name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.C2w3YfBKjIRS07DP]
Escondido Mind (Constant)

effect->Spell Efecto: Hidden Mind.name: Spell Efecto: Escondido Mind
effect->Spell Efecto: Hidden Mind.description:
Granted by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.C2w3YfBKjIRS07DP]{Escondido Mind}

Obtienes a +4 bonificador de estado to saves against mental effects.

action->Communal Knowledge.name: Communal Knowledge
action->Communal Knowledge.description: El dragon mentally communes con todos su current active informants simultaneously. They learn el present state de todos el informants, as status, y cualquier nuevo information el informants tienen learned since ellos fueron last en communication. Fragments de extraneous information briefly remain after using Communal Knowledge; for el next hora, el dragon puede attempt @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} pruebas for cualquier skill con un modifier de +36.

action->Information Network.name: Information Network
action->Information Network.description: The dragon can attempt a SOCIETY check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} in place of a check to Gather Information, recalling INTELLIGENCE from prior informants.

action->+2 Status to All Saves vs. Occul.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Occult

action->Diplomatic Solution.name: Diplomatic Solution
action->Diplomatic Solution.description:
Desencadenante The dragon rolls initiative

Efecto The dragon affects all enemies it can see within 60 pies with calm heightened to half the dragon's level rounded up (@Check[will|dc:42]). The dragon doesn't need to Sustain this effect, but if the dragon takes any hostile action against those affected, it breaks the effect for all criaturas.

action->Distracting Whisper.name: Distracting Whisper
action->Distracting Whisper.description:
Desencadenante The dragon is targeted with an attack

Efecto A mysterious voice whispers something disconcerting in the triggering criatura's ear, inflicting a –2 penalización de circunstancia to el ataque desencadenante.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.qsvSWxRqVQofjDdH]{Efecto: Distracting Whisper}

action->Cogitation Breath.name: Cogitation Breath
action->Cogitation Breath.description: The dragon unleashes a befuddling miasma, dealing @Damage[19d6[mental]|options:area-damage] daño in an @Template[type:cone|distance:80] (@Check[will|dc:42|basic] salvación). A criatura that fails its save is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} on a critical failure) for 1 minuto. The dragon can't use Cogitation Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Cogitation Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Draconic Frenzy.name: Frenesí Dracónico
action->Draconic Frenzy.description: El dragón realiza dos Golpes de garra y un Golpe de cola en cualquier orden.

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: El dragón recarga Cogitation Breath siempre que consigue un impacto crítico con un Golpe.

action->Steal Knowledge.name: Steal Knowledge
action->Steal Knowledge.description:
The dragon plucks a fragment of knowledge from the mind of a criatura within 60 pies, choosing a skill to affect. The criatura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:42] salvación.

Éxito The criatura is unaffected.

Fallo For the next minute, the criatura takes a –1 penalización de estado to checks using that skill, and the dragon gets a +1 bonificador de estado to using that skill.

Fallo crítico As failure, but the penalización is –2 and the bonus is +2.

action->Thought Whispers.name: Thought Whispers
action->Thought Whispers.description:
Frecuencia una vez por minuto

Efecto The dragon sends their mind out to seek others' thoughts, affecting all criaturas within 80 pies with mind reading (@Check[will|dc:42]).

action->Unveil Secret.name: Unveil Secret
action->Unveil Secret.description: The dragon delves into the mind of a criatura within 60 pies, learning something they'd find embarrassing or shameful unless they succeed at a @Check[will|dc:42] salvación. El objetivo becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 1} and cannot reduce their asustado condition for 1 minuto or until the dragon reveals the secret. As a reaction when the affected criatura attempts a check, the dragon can reveal their secret to discomfit them, requiring them to roll twice and take the lower result; this is a misfortune effect.

Wish Archdragon.name: Wish Archdragon
Wish Archdragon.publicNotes:
What es un wish? Un wish dragon would call ello el truest expression de self—cada individual wish reveals something de deep importance a el wisher, y no two wishes son ever quite el mismo. Whether el wish es one de creation o destruction, justice o vengeance, love o hate, wish dragones seek a understand what makes ello important a el wisher y view su ability a make ello un reality as un gift que helps them make sentido de el world.

To un wish dragon, learning what someone wishes for es el beginning de un conversation, granting them que wish es un gift, y watching what ellos do con ello es un reward. They reciben cada part de este journey seriously y spend much de su lives moviendose among otro ancestries a better understand what others want y need, especially during su younger anos. Mientras ellos view este mission as un righteous one, ello puede quedan todos-consuming, y some tienen been known a pierden todos sentido de themselves en su quest a bring about el dreams y desires de those around them.

spell->Truespeech (constant).name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SwUiVavHKMWG7t5K]
Truespeech (constant)

spell->Creation (at will).name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.TUj8eugNqAvB1vVR]
Creación (a voluntad)

action->+2 Status to All Saves vs. Arcan.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Arcane

action->Best Wishes.name: Best Wishes
action->Best Wishes.description: 40 pies. Being near a wish dragon gives other criaturas a greater sense of what they truly wish for, bolstering their sense of purpose while also distracting them from the task at hand. Las criaturas in the aura take a –1 penalización de estado to Perception but gain a +2 bonificador de estado to Will tiradas de salvación against mental effects. The wish dragon can't gain the benefit of their own aura or other actions that use the aura, and they can elige to exclude any criaturas from any benefit of the aura or action that uses the aura.

action->Dying Wish.name: Dying Wish
action->Dying Wish.description:
Frecuencia una vez al día

Desencadenante The dragon is reduced to 0 Puntos de Golpe

Efecto The dragon wishes to survive by any means necessary. The dragon is instead reduced to 1 Hit Point and teleports up to 10 miles away.

action->Wished Away.name: Wished Away
action->Wished Away.description:
Desencadenante The dragon is critically hit by an attack

Efecto The dragon wishes not to be hurt by this attack, gaining resistance 25 to all daño against el ataque desencadenante.

action->Breath of Loss.name: Breath of Loss
action->Breath of Loss.description: The dragon breathes a warm, gentle breeze of mist that creates the feeling of when deepest desires are achieved. As the breeze dissipates, the feeling of loss overwhelms criaturas' senses, dealing @Damage[22d6[mental]|options:area-damage] daño in a @Template[type:cone|distance:60] (@Check[will|dc:45] salvación). A criatura that critically fails its save is also consumed with the memory of the moment and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2}. The wish dragon can't use Breath of Loss again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Breath of Loss]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Destructive Wish.name: Destructive Wish
action->Destructive Wish.description:
Requisitos An illusion from Wish Come True is currently active

Efecto The wish dragon Dismisses the illusion of Wish Come True, which shatters into magical fragments, dealing @Damage[10d6[force]|options:area-damage] daño with a @Check[reflex|dc:45|basic] salvación to all criaturas in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:50] of the illusion.

action->Draconic Frenzy.name: Frenesí Dracónico
action->Draconic Frenzy.description: El dragón realiza dos Golpes de garra y un Golpe de cola en cualquier orden.

action->Draconic Momentum.name: Impulso dracónico
action->Draconic Momentum.description: The dragon recharges Breath of Loss siempre que they score a impacto crítico with a Golpe.

action->Wish Come True.name: Wish Come True
action->Wish Come True.description:
Frecuencia once per 10 minutos

Efecto The dragon creates an illusion in an unoccupied square within 60 pies that appears to all other criaturas that can see it to be the manifestation of their deepest material desire. Este has the effects of illusory object (though the illusion might appear to be a criatura to certain people) that last for 10 minutos. The wish dragon can Dismiss the illusion. Each non-wish dragon criatura who begins their turn within 200 pies in line of sight of the illusion must attempt a @Check[will|dc:45] salvación. If any criatura within reach of the illusion Interacts to touch it, the illusion ends and that criatura is invigorated, gaining 3d6 Puntos de Golpe temporales that last for 1 minuto.

Éxito crítico The criatura disbelieves the illusion and becomes temporarily immune to Wish Come True for 1 hora.

Éxito The criatura is unaffected.

Fallo The criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 asalto.

Fallo crítico The criatura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 asalto.

action->Wish You Would.name: Wish Tú Would
action->Wish You Would.description:
Requisitos An illusion from Wish Come True is active

Efecto The dragon targets one criatura within 200 pies currently stupefied by Wish Come True, making them believe that the object of their desires is under attack from all those around them and the dragon is the only one they can trust. El objetivo must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:44] Save or they become controlled by the dragon for 1 minuto. El objetivo may attempt a new save at the end of each of their turns. If the illusion from Wish Come True dissipates, their controlled state immediately ends.

Wyrmwraith.name: Espectro del Wyrm
Wyrmwraith.publicNotes:
Dahak's defiance and his hatred for all of creation brought loss to dragonkind. It is said that the first wyrmwraiths rose from the souls of dragons hurled into the Void by Dahak, but whether this is true or not is still a matter of debate. What is undeniable is that the wyrmwraiths are unliving conduits of the Void, shaped but unshackled by the plane's hunger for indiscriminate destruction.

Wyrmwraiths dwell in remote areas marred by catastrophes and death, where they can better hide their undead NATURE or indulge in their grim research. Their lairs often have a single, hidden and highly defensible antechamber where the wyrmwraith confers with its agents as it engages in a war with distant rivals through expendable proxies. Este dimly lit antechamber is usually filled with death and many undead servants, some raised from the bodies of those whose usefulness has come to an end.

Wyrmwraiths might enter temporary alliances with other undead, cults, or necromancers, especially when it comes to unearthing powerful secrets or striking a blow against a common powerful threat. While wyrmwraiths take great pleasure in acting against those who wield the power of the gods, often targeting them first in battle to rend their flesh and protective conjuros with their claws, they are often very cautious, striking only after stacking the odds in their favor.

Yeongno.name: Yeongno
Yeongno.publicNotes:
Neither human nor beast yet resembling both, yeongno (yeong-no) are criaturas that once were denizens of heaven but were cast out, down to the mortal Universe, due to their own greed. Yeongno claim to have once been celestial dragons and wear elongated dragon masks with full-body wraps decorated with scale patterns in honor of this claim—though no one has been able to confirm the veracity of this belief. As they wander, they hold a willow pipe in their mouths, producing a distinct "bibi" sound that often heralds their appearance.

Despite their reputation as monsters who eat people, yeongno are welcomed by the poor and oppressed, who see the criaturas as wise and just. Yeongno believe that by eating 100 wealthy individuals who abuse their wealth or who accumulated their wealth by underhanded or exploitative means, they can atone for their own greed, allowing them to ascend back into heaven. A corrupt and greedy individual can escape their fate of being eaten by a yeongno by giving away all of their wealth and agreeing to be transformed into a pig for one year. If the person can endure one year living as a pig in the care of a household they once harmed, the yeongno will spare them.
Yeongno.privateNotes:
Glutton's Redemption

Yeongno eat the corrupt and wealthy as a symbolic means of consuming their own greed. While yeongno aspire to ascend from their current existence, they also actively sabotage other criaturas hoping to do the same. They feel particularly threatened by imugi, whom the yeongno believe would take their spots in heaven.

Young Linnorm.name: Young Linnorm
Young Linnorm.publicNotes: Female linnorms lay eggs in the wilderness, where linnorms are known to hunt. A linnorm egg remains viable for many years, protected by a tough, leathery skin easily mistaken for stone. When a male linnorm eventually stumbles across the egg, he fertilizes it and takes it to a secure and remote location, leaving it alone to eventually hatch. Newborn linnorms remain hidden in their nests for several months as they mature, growing large enough to hunt on their own and setting out into the world. Estos linnorms are roughly the equivalent of older teenagers when compared to other species. Younger linnorms, while still primal criaturas with a strong tie to the First World, haven't yet manifested most of their magical powers. They still can't breathe deadly fire or lightning or see invisible criaturas, and, most importantly, they can be slain without prompting the linnorm's legendario death curse. They do, however, have voracious appetites, consuming any living thing to fuel their rapid growth. A linnorm is most vulnerable during this time; scouts who find tracks of a young linnorm quickly muster a hunting party of stalwart and experienced warriors to track the criatura down and kill it quickly-before they draw the attention of the linnorm's father.

Zinba.name: Zinba
Zinba.publicNotes:
Commonly known as ghost serpents, zinbas are rare, amphibious snakes with healing abilities. They're of similar size to other large snakes, such as pythons, but have a distinct bright blue coloring with red-and-black patterned stripes along their backs. Este distinct coloration is easy to spot, but zinbas can swim through the wet mud and soft earth of their homes to avoid being tracked by all but the most skilled pursuers. Este elusiveness inspires their "ghost serpent" moniker.

A zinba can metabolize a unique additive for its venom that converts it from a deadly poison to a healing agent, which makes zinbas particularly valuable in the eyes of healers and poachers. There is a high demand for zinbas in many markets; live serpents fetch a hefty sum, but zinba eggs are especially valuable, as zinbas reared in captivity are less willful and more likely to eat in confinement. Their elusiveness, however, leads many to search for their dens instead, which are large pools of water among remote wetlands or underground hollows near bodies of water. The water of a zinba's pool also has minor but valuable healing qualities, but removing water from a den causes it to lose its healing properties after a few hours, so most who find a den attempt to immediately make use of it.

Even finding dens is a difficult prospect, since zinbas are particularly intelligent for animals and can recognize signs of travelers near their favored hiding places. When there are signs of danger, a zinba collapses its lair and flees to create another den elsewhere.
